# Page: Overview

# Overview

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [_assets/ESM3_README.md](_assets/ESM3_README.md)
- [_assets/esmc_graphic.png](_assets/esmc_graphic.png)
- [_assets/esmfold2_binder.png](_assets/esmfold2_binder.png)
- [_assets/esmfold2_folding.png](_assets/esmfold2_folding.png)
- [_assets/header.png](_assets/header.png)
- [esm/__init__.py](esm/__init__.py)

</details>



The ESM repository is a comprehensive suite for protein biology, providing state-of-the-art models for representation learning, structure prediction, and de novo design. It serves as a scientific engine that leverages evolutionary data to map biological relationships across scales—from atomic interactions to billion-year evolutionary spans [README.md:10-12]().

The codebase supports three primary model families:
1.  **ESMC**: A state-of-the-art protein language model that has learned representations of protein biology from training on billions of protein sequences [README.md:12-13]().
2.  **ESM3**: A frontier generative model for biology, able to jointly reason across three fundamental biological properties of proteins: sequence, structure, and function [_assets/ESM3_README.md:3-4]().
3.  **ESMFold2**: A state-of-the-art structure prediction model built on the ESMC 6B model, validated for the design of protein-protein interactions [README.md:21-22]().

## Execution Modes

The system is designed for flexibility, offering two primary execution paths:

*   **Local Inference**: Users can run models locally using the `transformers` library or native ESM implementations. This is ideal for fine-tuning or high-throughput tasks where local GPU resources are available [README.md:57-89](), [_assets/ESM3_README.md:50-87]().
*   **Remote (Biohub Platform)**: High-level SDK clients connect to the Biohub Platform (formerly "Forge") via an API key. This mode abstracts away infrastructure requirements and provides access to hosted model variants [README.md:96-126](), [_assets/ESM3_README.md:32-48]().

For detailed setup instructions, see [Getting Started & Installation](#1.1).

## System Architecture

The repository is structured to bridge high-level biological concepts (proteins, complexes) with low-level tensor operations. The following diagram illustrates how core SDK entities relate to the underlying model implementations.

### SDK to Model Mapping
"This diagram shows how SDK clients map to specific model architectures and their corresponding entry points."

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "SDK Interface Layer"
        ESMC_Client[esm.sdk.esmc_client] --> ESMCInferenceClient[ESMCInferenceClient]
        ESMFold2_Client[esm.sdk.esmfold2_client] --> ESMFold2InferenceClient[ESMFold2InferenceClient]
        Client[esm.sdk.client] --> ESM3InferenceClient[ESM3InferenceClient]
    end

    subgraph "Model Implementations"
        ESMCInferenceClient -- "Local (Hugging Face)" --> ESMC_Model[esm.models.esmc.ESMC]
        ESMCInferenceClient -- "Remote (Biohub Platform)" --> ESMCForgeClient[esm.sdk.forge.ESMCForgeInferenceClient]
        
        ESMFold2InferenceClient -- "Remote (Biohub Platform)" --> SequenceStructureForgeClient[esm.sdk.forge.SequenceStructureForgeInferenceClient]
        
        ESM3InferenceClient -- "Local (Hugging Face)" --> ESM3_Model[esm.models.esm3.ESM3]
        ESM3InferenceClient -- "Remote (Biohub Platform)" --> ESM3ForgeClient[esm.sdk.forge.ESM3ForgeInferenceClient]
    end

    subgraph "Data Structures"
        ESMProtein_DS[esm.sdk.api.ESMProtein] --> ESMProteinTensor_DS[ESMProteinTensor]
        MolecularComplex_DS[esm.data.molecular_complex.MolecularComplex] --> StructurePredictionInput_DS[esm.data.esmfold2_input_builder.StructurePredictionInput]
    end
```
**Sources:** [README.md:112-126](), [_assets/ESM3_README.md:43-48](), [_assets/ESM3_README.md:62-65]()

## Model Families

The repository provides specialized architectures for different biological tasks.

| Model Family | Primary Purpose | Key Components |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **ESMC** | Sequence Embeddings | `ESMC`, `EsmSequenceTokenizer`, Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) [README.md:12-13](), [README.md:139-141]() |
| **ESM3** | Multimodal Generation | `ESM3`, `TransformerStack`, `TokenizerCollection` [_assets/ESM3_README.md:3-4](), [_assets/ESM3_README.md:10]() |
| **ESMFold2** | Structure Prediction | `ESMFold2InputBuilder`, Diffusion-based folding [README.md:21-22]() |

For a comparison of capabilities and parameter scales, see [Model Families & Capabilities](#1.2).

## Core Subsystems

The codebase is organized into several functional domains that handle the lifecycle of protein data:

1.  **Protein Representations**: Classes like `ESMProtein` and `MolecularComplex` handle raw data parsing (PDB/mmCIF) and geometric utilities.
2.  **Tokenization**: A multi-track system that discretizes sequences, 3D structures (via VQ-VAE), and functional annotations into discrete tokens for transformer processing.
3.  **Inference SDK**: A unified interface (`esm.sdk`) for interacting with models regardless of the backend (Local, Biohub Platform, or SageMaker) [README.md:112-124](), [_assets/ESM3_README.md:32-48]().
4.  **Generation Engine**: Logic for iterative masked language modeling (MLM) and diffusion-based sampling used in de novo design [_assets/ESM3_README.md:5-6]().

### Data Flow Overview
"The transformation from raw protein data to model-ready tensors."

```mermaid
graph LR
    PDB_mmCIF["PDB/mmCIF Files"] -- "Load (e.g., ProteinChain.from_pdb)" --> ProteinChain_Obj[ProteinChain]
    ProteinChain_Obj -- "Build input (ESMFold2InputBuilder)" --> MolecularComplex_Obj[MolecularComplex]
    MolecularComplex_Obj -- "Tokenize & Encode (esm.sdk.api.ESM3InferenceClient.encode)" --> ESMProteinTensor_Obj[esm.sdk.api.ESMProteinTensor]
    ESMProteinTensor_Obj -- "Model Forward Pass (esm.models.esm3.ESM3.forward)" --> TransformerStack_Output[TransformerStack Output]
    TransformerStack_Output -- "Output Heads" --> Model_Outputs[Logits / Coordinates / Other Predictions]
```
**Sources:** [README.md:128-131](), [_assets/ESM3_README.md:5-6](), [_assets/ESM3_README.md:77-79]()

# Page: Getting Started & Installation

# Getting Started & Installation

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [pixi.lock](pixi.lock)
- [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml)

</details>



This page provides a comprehensive guide to setting up the ESM repository for development and research. It covers environment configuration using `pixi` and `pip`, authentication for remote inference, and the fundamental data flow between local environments and the Biohub Platform.

## 1. Environment Setup

The ESM repository supports two primary installation methods: **Pixi** (recommended for development) and **Pip** (for integration into existing environments). The project requires Python 3.12 [pyproject.toml:6-6]().

### Method A: Pixi (Recommended)
`pixi` is used to manage reproducible environments, handling both Python dependencies and system-level requirements like `cmake` and `pkg-config` [pyproject.toml:73-78]().

1.  **Install Pixi**: Follow the instructions at [pixi.sh](https://pixi.sh).
2.  **Initialize Environment**:
    ```bash
    pixi install
    ```
    This command reads `pyproject.toml` and `pixi.lock` to create a locked environment in the `.pixi` directory [pyproject.toml:68-71]().
3.  **Activate Shell**:
    ```bash
    pixi shell
    ```

### Method B: Pip
If you prefer standard pip, ensure you have Python 3.12 installed.
```bash
pip install esm@git+https://github.com/Biohub/esm.git@main
```
*Note: The project depends on a specific fork of the `transformers` library [pyproject.toml:25-25]().*

### Core Dependencies
The following key libraries are required for ESM operations:
| Library | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- |
| `torch` | Neural network backend (>=2.2.0) [pyproject.toml:24-24]() |
| `transformers` | Hugging Face models, specifically a Biohub fork [pyproject.toml:25-25]() |
| `biotite` | Protein structure parsing and manipulation [pyproject.toml:28-28]() |
| `rdkit` | Handling small molecules and ligands [pyproject.toml:29-29]() |
| `msgpack-numpy` | Efficient serialization for API requests [pyproject.toml:30-30]() |
| `ipywidgets` | Powering the interactive Jupyter UI [pyproject.toml:40-40]() |

Sources: [pyproject.toml:24-47]()

---

## 2. Configuration & Authentication

ESM supports both local model execution and remote inference via the Biohub Platform (Forge). To use remote inference, you must configure an API key.

### API Key Configuration
The SDK looks for the `ESM_API_KEY` environment variable. You can set this in your shell or via a `.env` file.

```bash
export ESM_API_KEY="your_api_key_here"
```

### Execution Modes
The system is designed to be backend-agnostic through the `esm.sdk` interfaces.

| Mode | Description | Implementation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Local** | Models run on your local GPU/CPU. | Uses `esm.models` and `torch`. |
| **Remote** | Models run on Biohub Forge or SageMaker. | Uses `SequenceStructureForgeInferenceClient`. |

### System Initialization Flow
The following diagram illustrates how the environment and configuration are used to initialize a client.

**Client Initialization Architecture**
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Environment Space"
        ENV_VAR["ESM_API_KEY"]
        PIXI_LOCK["pixi.lock"]
        PYPROJ["pyproject.toml"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space (esm.sdk)"
        CLIENT_FACTORY["esm.sdk.client()"]
        FORGE_CLIENT["SequenceStructureForgeInferenceClient"]
        LOCAL_CLIENT["LocalInferenceClient (Experimental)"]
    end

    ENV_VAR -.->|"Auth"| FORGE_CLIENT
    PYPROJ -->|"Metadata"| CLIENT_FACTORY
    PIXI_LOCK -->|"Runtime Env"| CLIENT_FACTORY
    
    CLIENT_FACTORY -->|"Returns"| FORGE_CLIENT
    CLIENT_FACTORY -->|"Returns"| LOCAL_CLIENT
```
Sources: [pyproject.toml:1-47](), [README.md:99-102]()

---

## 3. Running Your First Example

Once installed, you can verify the setup by running a simple sequence embedding or structure prediction.

### Local Inference Example
The repository includes a `cookbook` directory with scripts for local execution. For ESMC, you can use the Hugging Face `transformers` library directly.

```python
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForMaskedLM, AutoTokenizer
from huggingface_hub import login

# login with your Hugging Face credentials
login()

# example GFP sequence
sequences = ["MSKGEELFTGVVPILVELDGDVNGHKFSVSGEGEGDATYGKLTLKFICTTGKLPVPWPTLVTTFSYGVQCFSRYPDHMKQHDFFKSAMPEGYVQERTIFFKDDGNYKTRAEVKFEGDTLVNRIELKGIDFKEDGNILGHKLEYNYNSHNVYIMADKQKNGIKVNFKIRHNIEDGSVQLADHYQQNTPIGDGPVLLPDNHYLSTQSALSKDPNEKRDHMVLLEFVTAAGITHGMDELYK"]

model = AutoModelForMaskedLM.from_pretrained(
    "biohub/ESMC-6B",
    device_map="auto",
).eval()
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("biohub/ESMC-6B")

inputs = tokenizer(sequences, return_tensors="pt", padding=True)
inputs = {k: v.to(model.device) for k, v in inputs.items()}
with torch.inference_mode():
    output = model(**inputs)

# To return hidden states from all transformer layers:
# output = model(**inputs, output_hidden_states=True)
```
Sources: [README.md:69-94]()

### Remote SDK Example
Using the SDK to interact with ESMC via the Biohub Platform:

```python
from esm.sdk import esmc_client
from esm.sdk.api import ESMProtein, LogitsConfig

# Human carbonic anhydrase II (PDB 2CBA)
protein = ESMProtein(
    sequence=(
        "MSHHWGYGKHNGPEHWHKDFPIAKGERQSPVDIDTHTAKYDPSLKPLSVSYDQATSLRILNNGHAFNVEFDD"
        "SQDKAVLKGGPLDGTYRLIQFHFHWGSLDGQGSEHTVDKKKYAAELHLVHWNTKYGDFGKAVQQPDGLAVL"
        "GIFLKVGSAKPGLQKVVDVLDSIKTKGKSADFTNFDPRGLLPESLDYWTYPGSLTTPPLLECVTWIVLKEP"
        "ISVSSEQVLKFRKLNFNGEGEPEELMVDNWRPAQPLKNRQIKASFK"
    )
)
model = esmc_client(
    model="esmc-600m-2024-12", url="https://biohub.ai", token="<your API token>"
)

protein_tensor = model.encode(protein)
logits_output = model.logits(
    protein_tensor, LogitsConfig(sequence=True, return_embeddings=True)
)

print(logits_output.logits, logits_output.embeddings)
```
Sources: [README.md:112-134]()

## 4. Development Workflow

### Code Quality Tools
The project uses `ruff` for linting and `ty` (a type checker) for type checking, managed via `pre-commit` [pyproject.toml:104-140]().

*   **Linting**: `pixi run lint-all` [pyproject.toml:97-97]()
*   **Testing**: `pytest` is configured to ignore specific client tests that require remote credentials by default [pyproject.toml:49-55]().

### Testing Architecture
The test suite is split between unit tests and integration tests.

**Testing and CI Data Flow**
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Local Development"
        PRE_COMMIT["pre-commit (ruff/ty)"]
        PYTEST["pytest -n auto"]
    end

    subgraph "CI/CD (GitHub Actions)"
        TEST_ESM["job: test-esm"]
        DOCKER_BUILD["Makefile (Docker Build)"]
    end

    PRE_COMMIT -->|"Success"| PYTEST
    PYTEST -->|"Push"| TEST_ESM
    TEST_ESM -->|"Integration"| DOCKER_BUILD
```
Sources: [pyproject.toml:49-55](), [pyproject.toml:89-98](), [pyproject.toml:104-140]()

# Page: Model Families & Capabilities

# Model Families & Capabilities

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [esm/models/function_decoder.py](esm/models/function_decoder.py)
- [esm/pretrained.py](esm/pretrained.py)

</details>



This page provides a technical comparison of the three primary model families within the ESM ecosystem: **ESMC**, **ESM3**, and **ESMFold2**. These models represent a transition from sequence-only language modeling to multimodal protein design and high-fidelity structure prediction.

## Overview of Model Families

The repository supports two execution modes for these models: **Local Inference** (via Hugging Face weights and local PyTorch execution) and **Remote Inference** (via the Biohub Platform API).

| Feature | ESMC | ESM3 | ESMFold2 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Primary Task** | Sequence Representation | Multimodal Design/Generation | Structure Prediction |
| **Architecture** | Transformer (Sequence) | Multimodal Transformer | Diffusion-based Folding |
| **Inputs** | Amino Acid Sequence | Seq, Struct, SS8, SASA, Func | Seq, MSA, Templates |
| **Scale Variants** | 300M, 600M, 6B | Open Small (v1) | 6B Backbone |
| **Key Use Case** | Embeddings, Variant Effect | De novo design, Inverse folding | High-accuracy folding |

Sources: [README.md:10-37](), [esm/utils/constants/models.py:2-13]()

---

## ESMC: Sequence Embedding Model

ESMC is the latest generation of protein language models, optimized for learning biological representations from billions of sequences [README.md:10-12](). It serves as the foundation for the ESM Atlas and SAE-based interpretability [README.md:35-37]().

### Architecture & Implementation
ESMC utilizes a standard Transformer backbone with support for **Flash Attention** to handle long-range structural dependencies efficiently [esm/models/esmc.py:61-74]().

*   **Class**: `ESMC` [esm/models/esmc.py:45-45]()
*   **Backbone**: `TransformerStack` [esm/models/esmc.py:67-74]()
*   **Output**: `ESMCOutput` containing `sequence_logits`, `embeddings`, and `hidden_states` [esm/models/esmc.py:38-42]()

### Model Scales & Factory Functions
Models can be instantiated locally using the `ESMC.from_pretrained()` method or specific factory functions in `esm.pretrained`.

| Model Constant | Parameters | Factory Function |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ESMC_300M` | 300 Million | `ESMC_300M_202412` [esm/pretrained.py:66-77]() |
| `ESMC_600M` | 600 Million | `ESMC_600M_202412` [esm/pretrained.py:79-90]() |
| `ESMC_6B` | 6 Billion | `ESMC_6B_202412` [esm/pretrained.py:92-105]() |

Sources: [esm/models/esmc.py:79-96](), [esm/pretrained.py:66-105](), [esm/utils/constants/models.py:9-11]()

---

## ESM3: Multimodal Protein Language Model

ESM3 is a generative world model capable of reasoning across multiple "tracks" of protein data simultaneously [esm/models/esm3.py:188-190](). It uses a unified vocabulary to represent sequence, structure (via VQ-VAE tokens), and function [esm/models/esm3.py:62-102]().

### Data Flow & Component Mapping
The following diagram illustrates how the `ESM3` class coordinates various sub-models to process multimodal inputs.

**ESM3 Multimodal Integration**
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Input Space"
        SEQ["Sequence Tokens"]
        STR["Structure Tokens"]
        FUNC["Function Tokens"]
        SS8["SS8 / SASA Tokens"]
    end

    subgraph "ESM3 Class [esm/models/esm3.py]"
        EI["EncodeInputs"]
        TS["TransformerStack"]
        OH["OutputHeads"]
    end

    subgraph "Specialized Decoders"
        STD["StructureTokenDecoder"]
        FTD["FunctionTokenDecoder"]
    end

    SEQ --> EI
    STR --> EI
    FUNC --> EI
    SS8 --> EI
    
    EI --> TS
    TS --> OH
    
    OH -->|"structure_logits"| STD
    OH -->|"function_logits"| FTD
```
Sources: [esm/models/esm3.py:62-185](), [esm/models/esm3.py:211-218]()

### Key Components
*   **`EncodeInputs`**: Projects all tracks (Sequence, pLDDT, Structure, SS8, SASA, Function, Residue) into a shared `d_model` embedding space [esm/models/esm3.py:62-148]().
*   **`StructureTokenEncoder/Decoder`**: A VQ-VAE that discretizes 3D coordinates into 4096 discrete tokens [esm/models/vqvae.py:179-187](), [esm/utils/constants/esm3.py:13-20]().
*   **`FunctionTokenDecoder`**: Decodes function tokens into InterPro annotations and keyword TF-IDF vectors [esm/models/function_decoder.py:54-125]().

Sources: [esm/models/esm3.py:15-16](), [esm/pretrained.py:108-125]()

---

## ESMFold2: All-Atom Structure Prediction

ESMFold2 is built upon the ESMC 6B backbone and is optimized for predicting the structures of complex biological systems, including proteins, nucleic acids (DNA/RNA), and small-molecule ligands [README.md:21-28]().

### Capabilities
*   **Multi-chain Support**: Can fold protein-protein, protein-nucleic acid, and antibody-antigen complexes [cookbook/tutorials/esmfold2.ipynb:15-18]().
*   **Non-canonical Support**: Handles non-canonical amino acids via CCD codes and covalent modifications [cookbook/tutorials/esmfold2.ipynb:19-22]().
*   **MSA Integration**: Supports Multiple Sequence Alignments to improve prediction accuracy [cookbook/tutorials/esmfold2.ipynb:23-25]().

### System Architecture
The folding process is managed via the `ESMFold2InputBuilder` which assembles various molecular inputs into a `StructurePredictionInput` payload for the diffusion engine.

**ESMFold2 Input Assembly**
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "User Inputs [esm/utils/structure/input_builder.py]"
        PI["ProteinInput"]
        DI["DNAInput / RNAInput"]
        LI["LigandInput"]
        MSA["MSA Data"]
    end

    subgraph "Builder Logic"
        IB["ESMFold2InputBuilder"]
        SPI["StructurePredictionInput"]
    end

    subgraph "Inference Client [esm/sdk/api.py]"
        FC["esmfold2_client"]
        FAA["fold_all_atom()"]
    end

    PI --> IB
    DI --> IB
    LI --> IB
    MSA --> IB
    
    IB --> SPI
    SPI --> FAA
    FC --> FAA
```
Sources: [cookbook/tutorials/esmfold2.ipynb:79-81](), [esm/utils/constants/models.py:12-14]()

---

## Model Selection Guide

| If you want to... | Use This Model | Implementation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Generate a new protein sequence for a specific fold | **ESM3** | `esm.models.esm3.ESM3` |
| Extract features for a downstream classifier | **ESMC** | `esm.models.esmc.ESMC` |
| Predict the 3D structure of a protein-DNA complex | **ESMFold2** | `esm.sdk.esmfold2_client` |
| Interpret model features using SAEs | **ESMC** | `esm.models.esmc.ESMC` |
| Perform inverse folding (Structure $\rightarrow$ Sequence) | **ESM3** | `ESM3.forward_and_sample` |

Sources: [README.md:10-37](), [esm/models/esm3.py:188-190](), [esm/models/esmc.py:45-48]()

# Page: Core Model Architectures

# Core Model Architectures

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [esm/layers/transformer_stack.py](esm/layers/transformer_stack.py)
- [esm/models/esm3.py](esm/models/esm3.py)
- [esm/models/esmc.py](esm/models/esmc.py)
- [esm/utils/structure/input_builder.py](esm/utils/structure/input_builder.py)

</details>



This page provides a high-level technical overview of the neural network architectures that power the ESM ecosystem. The codebase supports three primary model families: **ESM3**, a multimodal generative model; **ESMC**, a sequence-only transformer; and **ESMFold2**, a diffusion-based structure prediction model. These models are built upon a shared library of optimized transformer layers and specialized tokenizers.

## Architectural Overview

The ESM repository transitions from traditional protein language modeling to a multimodal, multi-track architecture. While **ESMC** focuses on high-efficiency sequence embeddings, **ESM3** integrates sequence, structure, and function into a unified transformer backbone. **ESMFold2** extends these capabilities to high-fidelity all-atom structure prediction.

### Component Relationship Diagram
The following diagram illustrates how the core classes and modules interact to process protein data across different model families.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Input Processing"
        Protein[ESMProtein] -->|encode| SDK[ESMProteinTensor]
        SDK -->|tokenize| Tokens[Track Tokens]
    end

    subgraph "ESM3 Multimodal Architecture"
        Tokens --> EncodeInputs["esm.models.esm3.EncodeInputs"]
        EncodeInputs --> TStack3["esm.layers.transformer_stack.TransformerStack"]
        TStack3 --> OutputHeads["esm.models.esm3.OutputHeads"]
        OutputHeads --> ESMOutput["esm.models.esm3.ESMOutput"]
    end

    subgraph "ESMC Sequence Architecture"
        Tokens --> Embed["nn.Embedding"]
        Embed --> TStackC["esm.layers.transformer_stack.TransformerStack"]
        TStackC --> SeqHead["esm.layers.regression_head.RegressionHead"]
        SeqHead --> ESMCOutput["esm.models.esmc.ESMCOutput"]
    end

    subgraph "Structure Subsystems"
        ESMOutput -->|structure_logits| VQVAE_Dec["esm.models.vqvae.StructureTokenDecoder"]
        VQVAE_Dec -->|backbone| Affine["esm.utils.structure.affine3d.Affine3D"]
    end

    subgraph "Function Subsystems"
        ESMOutput -->|function_logits| FuncDec["esm.models.function_decoder.FunctionTokenDecoder"]
    end
```
**Sources:** [esm/models/esm3.py:62-185](), [esm/models/esmc.py:45-191](), [esm/models/vqvae.py:179-205](), [esm/models/function_decoder.py:54-125]()

---

## ESM3: Multimodal Generative Model

**ESM3** is a multimodal transformer designed to reason across different "tracks" of protein information simultaneously. It treats proteins as a collection of synchronized sequences: amino acids, structural coordinates (discretized), secondary structure, solvent accessibility, and functional annotations.

*   **Multimodal Embedding:** The `EncodeInputs` class [esm/models/esm3.py:62-148]() sums embeddings from all tracks, including sequence, structure tokens, SS8, SASA, and function tokens.
*   **Transformer Backbone:** A `TransformerStack` [esm/layers/transformer_stack.py:11-20]() processes the combined embeddings using rotary position embeddings and optional Flash Attention.
*   **Output Heads:** The `OutputHeads` class [esm/models/esm3.py:151-185]() provides independent regression heads for every input track, enabling the model to predict or "fill in" masked values for any modality.

For a deep dive into the multimodal tracks and forward pass, see **[ESM3 – Multimodal Protein Language Model](#2.1)**.

---

## ESMC: Efficient Sequence Embeddings

**ESMC** (ESM Central) is a sequence-only transformer architecture optimized for scale and speed. It is the successor to the ESM-2 family, providing state-of-the-art embeddings for downstream tasks and masked language modeling.

*   **Optimized Attention:** ESMC natively supports `unpad_input` and `pad_input` logic [esm/models/esmc.py:151-180]() to handle variable-length sequences efficiently when using Flash Attention.
*   **Variants:** Available in 300M, 600M, and 6B parameter variants [esm/models/esmc.py:80-96]().
*   **Output:** Returns `ESMCOutput` [esm/models/esmc.py:37-42]() containing logits, embeddings, and optionally all hidden states and attention maps.

For details on the sequence-only architecture and Flash Attention integration, see **[ESMC – Sequence Embedding Model](#2.2)**.

---

## ESMFold2: Structure Prediction

**ESMFold2** is a diffusion-based structure prediction model. Unlike the original ESMFold, which used a folding trunk, ESMFold2 leverages a diffusion process to generate all-atom coordinates.

*   **Input Handling:** Uses `StructurePredictionInput` [esm/utils/structure/input_builder.py:75-79]() to construct complex payloads including MSAs, ligands, and multi-chain information. The `serialize_structure_prediction_input` function [esm/utils/structure/input_builder.py:82-154]() handles serialization.
*   **Complex Support:** Natively handles `ProteinInput`, `DNAInput`, `RNAInput`, and `LigandInput` [esm/utils/structure/input_builder.py:22-50]().
*   **Diffusion Pipeline:** Operates on `StructurePredictionInput` to iteratively refine atomic positions.

For details on the diffusion pipeline and multi-chain support, see **[ESMFold2 – All-Atom Structure Prediction](#2.3)**.

---

## Support Architectures: VQ-VAE & Function Decoders

To enable the transformer to "see" and "write" 3D structures and complex functions, ESM3 utilizes specialized compression and expansion models.

### Structure VQ-VAE
The `StructureTokenEncoder` and `StructureTokenDecoder` [esm/models/vqvae.py:179-205]() implement a Vector Quantized Variational Autoencoder.
*   **Encoder:** Maps 3D coordinates to a discrete set of 4096 structure tokens using a `GeometricEncoderStack`.
*   **Decoder:** Reconstructs the protein backbone (`Affine3D`) from these discrete tokens.

### Function Decoder
The `FunctionTokenDecoder` [esm/models/function_decoder.py:54-125]() translates abstract function tokens into human-readable InterPro annotations and TF-IDF keyword vectors. It uses a `TransformerStack` to expand depth-8 function tokens into high-dimensional classification logits.

For details, see **[VQ-VAE Structure Tokenizer & Function Decoder](#2.4)**.

---

## Reusable Building Blocks

The models share a core library of neural network components located in `esm.layers`.

| Component | Description | File |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TransformerStack` | Reusable stack of transformer blocks with configurable geometry and attention. | [esm/layers/transformer_stack.py:10-61]() |
| `UnifiedTransformerBlock` | A single transformer layer supporting both plain and geometric attention. | [esm/layers/blocks.py]() |
| `RegressionHead` | Standard MLP head for projecting hidden states to output vocabularies. | [esm/layers/regression_head.py:13-24]() |
| `EMACodebook` | The quantization layer used in the Structure VQ-VAE. | [esm/layers/codebook.py]() |

For technical specifications of these layers, see **[Transformer Building Blocks](#2.5)**.

# Page: ESM3 – Multimodal Protein Language Model

# ESM3 – Multimodal Protein Language Model

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [esm/models/esm3.py](esm/models/esm3.py)
- [esm/models/function_decoder.py](esm/models/function_decoder.py)
- [esm/pretrained.py](esm/pretrained.py)
- [esm/utils/structure/affine3d.py](esm/utils/structure/affine3d.py)

</details>



ESM3 is a multimodal generative protein language model capable of reasoning across sequence, structure, and functional annotations. It is implemented as a transformer-based architecture that integrates multiple data tracks into a unified latent space, enabling tasks such as structure prediction, inverse folding, and functional design.

## ESM3 Architecture Overview

The `ESM3` class in `esm/models/esm3.py` serves as the primary implementation of the model. It inherits from `nn.Module` and implements the `ESM3InferenceClient` interface [esm/models/esm3.py:188-188](). The architecture consists of three main stages:
1.  **Input Encoding**: Projecting multimodal tracks (sequence, structure tokens, etc.) into a shared embedding.
2.  **Transformer Backbone**: A stack of unified transformer blocks supporting both standard and geometric attention.
3.  **Output Heads**: Regressing logits for each track from the final transformer hidden states.

### Data Flow and Code Entity Mapping

The following diagram maps the high-level multimodal data flow to the specific classes and modules within the ESM3 codebase.

**ESM3 Multimodal Pipeline**
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph InputSpace ["Input Space (ESMProteinTensor)"]
        SEQ["sequence_tokens"]
        STR["structure_tokens"]
        SS8["ss8_tokens"]
        SASA["sasa_tokens"]
        FUNC["function_tokens"]
        RES["residue_annotation_tokens"]
        AVG_PLDDT["average_plddt"]
        PER_RES_PLDDT["per_res_plddt"]
    end

    subgraph Encoder ["esm.models.esm3.EncodeInputs"]
        EI["EncodeInputs.forward()"]
        EMB_SEQ["sequence_embed (nn.Embedding)"]
        EMB_STR["structure_tokens_embed (nn.Embedding)"]
        EMB_SS8["ss8_embed (nn.Embedding)"]
        EMB_SASA["sasa_embed (nn.Embedding)"]
        EMB_FUNC["function_embed (nn.ModuleList)"]
        EMB_RES["residue_embed (nn.EmbeddingBag)"]
        PROJ_PLDDT["plddt_projection (nn.Linear)"]
        PROJ_PER_RES_PLDDT["structure_per_res_plddt_projection (nn.Linear)"]
    end

    subgraph Backbone ["esm.layers.transformer_stack.TransformerStack"]
        TS["TransformerStack.forward()"]
        UTB["UnifiedTransformerBlock"]
        GA["GeometricReasoningOriginalImpl"]
    end

    subgraph Heads ["esm.models.esm3.OutputHeads"]
        OH["OutputHeads.forward()"]
        RH_SEQ["sequence_head (RegressionHead)"]
        RH_STR["structure_head (RegressionHead)"]
        RH_SS8["ss8_head (RegressionHead)"]
        RH_SASA["sasa_head (RegressionHead)"]
        RH_FUNC["function_head (RegressionHead)"]
        RH_RES["residue_head (RegressionHead)"]
    end

    SEQ --> EMB_SEQ
    STR --> EMB_STR
    SS8 --> EMB_SS8
    SASA --> EMB_SASA
    FUNC --> EMB_FUNC
    RES --> EMB_RES
    AVG_PLDDT --> PROJ_PLDDT
    PER_RES_PLDDT --> PROJ_PER_RES_PLDDT

    EMB_SEQ --> EI
    EMB_STR --> EI
    EMB_SS8 --> EI
    EMB_SASA --> EI
    EMB_FUNC --> EI
    EMB_RES --> EI
    PROJ_PLDDT --> EI
    PROJ_PER_RES_PLDDT --> EI

    EI -- "Summed Embeddings" --> TS
    TS -- "x (Post-Norm)" --> OH
    OH --> ESMO["ESMOutput"]

    Sources: [esm/models/esm3.py:62-148](), [esm/layers/transformer_stack.py:10-116](), [esm/models/esm3.py:151-185]()
```

**Sources:** [esm/models/esm3.py:62-185](), [esm/layers/transformer_stack.py:10-116]()

---

## Input Encoding (EncodeInputs)

The `EncodeInputs` module handles the initial projection of eight distinct tracks into a single $d_{model}$ vector per residue [esm/models/esm3.py:62-70]().

| Track | Token Source | Encoding Mechanism |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Sequence** | Amino Acid Tokens | `nn.Embedding(64, d_model)` [esm/models/esm3.py:74-74]() |
| **Structure** | VQ-VAE Tokens | `nn.Embedding(4096 + 5, d_model)` [esm/models/esm3.py:80-80]() |
| **SS8** | Secondary Structure | `nn.Embedding(8 + 3, d_model)` [esm/models/esm3.py:83-83]() |
| **SASA** | Solvent Accessibility | `nn.Embedding(16 + 3, d_model)` [esm/models/esm3.py:84-84]() |
| **Function** | InterPro LSH | `nn.ModuleList` of 8 `nn.Embedding` (dim $d/8$) [esm/models/esm3.py:87-89]() |
| **Residue** | Annotations | `nn.EmbeddingBag(1478, d_model, mode="sum", padding_idx=0)` [esm/models/esm3.py:91-91]() |
| **pLDDT** | Global/Per-Res | RBF kernels + `nn.Linear` projection [esm/models/esm3.py:106-112]() |

The forward pass sums these embeddings element-wise:
$$X_{input} = E_{seq} + E_{struct} + E_{ss8} + E_{sasa} + E_{func} + E_{res} + E_{plddt\_avg} + E_{plddt\_per\_res}$$
[esm/models/esm3.py:139-148]()

**Sources:** [esm/models/esm3.py:62-148]()

---

## Transformer Backbone and Geometric Conditioning

The backbone is a `TransformerStack` composed of `UnifiedTransformerBlock` layers [esm/models/esm3.py:212-212]().

### UnifiedTransformerBlock
Each block can perform two types of attention:
1.  **Standard Attention**: Multi-head attention (optionally using `FlashMultiHeadAttention`).
2.  **Geometric Attention**: Enabled via `use_geom_attn`. It uses `GeometricReasoningOriginalImpl` to incorporate 3D spatial relationships.

### Affine3D Conditioning
Geometric attention is conditioned on `Affine3D` frames, which represent the local coordinate system (orientation and position) of each residue [esm/models/esm3.py:255-265](). These frames are built from backbone coordinates during the forward pass using `build_affine3d_from_coordinates` [esm/utils/structure/affine3d.py:290-300]().

**Sources:** [esm/models/esm3.py:212-212](), [esm/models/esm3.py:255-265](), [esm/utils/structure/affine3d.py:290-300]()

---

## Output Heads and ESMOutput

The `OutputHeads` module contains `RegressionHead` instances for each input track [esm/models/esm3.py:151-160]().

*   **RegressionHead**: A standard block consisting of a Linear layer, GELU activation, LayerNorm, and a final Linear projection to the vocabulary size [esm/layers/regression_head.py:13-20]().
*   **ESMOutput**: A dataclass that aggregates the resulting logits for sequence, structure, SS8, SASA, function, and residue tracks, along with the final embeddings and optional attention weights [esm/models/esm3.py:50-59]().

**Sources:** [esm/models/esm3.py:50-59](), [esm/models/esm3.py:151-185](), [esm/layers/regression_head.py:13-20]()

---

## Pretrained Factory Functions

ESM3 models are typically instantiated using factory functions in `esm/pretrained.py` which handle architecture configuration and weight loading.

**Model Loading Logic**
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph Registry ["esm.pretrained.LOCAL_MODEL_REGISTRY"]
        R1["ESM3_OPEN_SMALL"]
    end

    subgraph Builder ["esm.pretrained.ESM3_sm_open_v0"]
        B1["Initialize ESM3 Architecture"]
        B2["Load weights (esm3_sm_open_v1.pth)"]
        B3["Attach Tokenizers"]
    end

    subgraph SubComponents ["Component Builders"]
        SE["ESM3_structure_encoder_v0"]
        SD["ESM3_structure_decoder_v0"]
        FD["ESM3_function_decoder_v0"]
    end

    R1 --> B1
    B1 --> SE
    B1 --> SD
    B1 --> FD
    B2 --> B3
    B3 --> Final["ESM3 Model Instance"]

    Sources: [esm/pretrained.py:108-136]()
```

Key factory functions include:
*   `ESM3_sm_open_v0`: Loads the open-source small ESM3 model (1.4B parameters, 48 layers, $d_{model}=1536$) [esm/pretrained.py:108-125]().
*   `ESM3_structure_encoder_v0` / `ESM3_structure_decoder_v0`: Loads the VQ-VAE components for structural tokenization [esm/pretrained.py:28-51]().
*   `ESM3_function_decoder_v0`: Loads the decoder for InterPro and keyword prediction [esm/pretrained.py:54-63]().

**Sources:** [esm/pretrained.py:28-136]()

---

## Forward Pass Implementation

The `ESM3.forward()` method orchestrates the multimodal data flow [esm/models/esm3.py:238-306]():

1.  **Coordinate Processing**: If raw coordinates are provided, it builds `Affine3D` frames and calculates per-residue pLDDT [esm/models/esm3.py:255-265]().
2.  **Encoding**: Calls `self.encoder` to generate the initial latent representation [esm/models/esm3.py:276-286]().
3.  **Transformer Stack**: Passes the embeddings through `self.transformer`, applying geometric attention if structural frames are present [esm/models/esm3.py:288-295]().
4.  **Heads**: Passes the transformer output to `self.heads` to generate `ESMOutput` [esm/models/esm3.py:297-306]().

**Sources:** [esm/models/esm3.py:238-306]()

---

# Page: ESMC – Sequence Embedding Model

# ESMC – Sequence Embedding Model

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [esm/layers/attention.py](esm/layers/attention.py)
- [esm/layers/blocks.py](esm/layers/blocks.py)
- [esm/models/esmc.py](esm/models/esmc.py)
- [esm/utils/misc.py](esm/utils/misc.py)
- [esm/utils/structure/input_builder.py](esm/utils/structure/input_builder.py)

</details>



The **ESMC** (Evolutionary Scale Modeling - Core) is a sequence-only transformer model designed for efficient protein sequence embedding and masked language modeling. Unlike the multimodal ESM3, ESMC focuses exclusively on the amino acid sequence track, utilizing a streamlined architecture that supports high-performance inference through Flash Attention and optimized variable-length sequence handling.

## Architecture Overview

The ESMC architecture consists of a sequence embedding layer, a stack of transformer blocks, and a regression head for sequence token prediction. It is implemented in the `ESMC` class, which inherits from both `nn.Module` and `ESMCInferenceClient` [esm/models/esmc.py:45-53]().

### Key Components

| Component | Description | Code Entity |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Embedding Layer** | Maps sequence tokens to the model's hidden dimension ($d_{model}$). | `self.embed` [esm/models/esmc.py:64]() |
| **Transformer Backbone** | A stack of transformer layers with optional Flash Attention support. | `self.transformer` [esm/models/esmc.py:67-74]() |
| **Sequence Head** | A regression head that predicts logits over the 64-token amino acid vocabulary. | `self.sequence_head` [esm/models/esmc.py:76]() |
| **Tokenizer** | Handles conversion between raw strings and integer tensors. | `self.tokenizer` [esm/models/esmc.py:77]()

Sources:
- [esm/models/esmc.py:45-78]()
- [esm/layers/transformer_stack.py:17-50]()

---

## Data Flow & Forward Pass

The ESMC forward pass is optimized for batching variable-length sequences. It employs a "pad-unpad" strategy when Flash Attention is enabled to avoid redundant computation on padding tokens.

### Sequence Processing Diagram

The following diagram illustrates the flow from raw sequence input to model output, highlighting the interaction between the `ESMC` class and the underlying `TransformerStack`.

**ESMC Sequence Processing Flow**
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Input Space"
        RAW["list[str] (Raw Sequences)"]
    end

    subgraph "ESMC Class [esm/models/esmc.py]"
        TOK["_tokenize()"]
        EMB["nn.Embedding (self.embed)"]
        UNPAD["unpad_input() (Flash Attention Only)"]
        TRANS["TransformerStack (self.transformer)"]
        PAD["pad_input()"]
        HEAD["RegressionHead (self.sequence_head)"]
    end

    subgraph "Output Space"
        OUT["ESMCOutput"]
    end

    RAW --> TOK
    TOK --> EMB
    EMB --> UNPAD
    UNPAD --> TRANS
    TRANS --> PAD
    PAD --> HEAD
    HEAD --> OUT
    TRANS -- "hidden_states" --> OUT
```

### Implementation Details
1.  **Tokenization**: Raw sequences are tokenized using `encoding.tokenize_sequence` and stacked into a batch using `stack_variable_length_tensors` [esm/models/esmc.py:106-115]().
2.  **Unpadding**: If `use_flash_attn` is True, the model uses `unpad_input` to flatten the batch into a single sequence of non-padding tokens [esm/models/esmc.py:151-163]().
3.  **Transformer Execution**: The `TransformerStack` processes the tokens. It uses `FlashMultiHeadAttention` if enabled, which requires a boolean `sequence_id` mask [esm/layers/attention.py:99-143]().
4.  **Repadding**: After the transformer blocks, the flattened tensors are restored to their original `[B, L, D]` shape using `pad_input` before being passed to the output head [esm/models/esmc.py:171-180]().

Sources:
- [esm/models/esmc.py:123-191]()
- [esm/layers/attention.py:99-143]()
- [esm/utils/misc.py:180-210]()

---

## Flash Attention & Variable Length Support

ESMC is built to handle the high-throughput requirements of protein sequence embedding. It integrates `flash_attn` for both memory efficiency and speed.

### Flash Attention Integration
The `FlashMultiHeadAttention` class [esm/layers/attention.py:99]() implements the optimized attention mechanism. It uses `TritonRotaryEmbedding` for positional encoding [esm/layers/attention.py:108]() and calls `flash_attn_varlen_qkvpacked_func` for the core computation [esm/layers/attention.py:138]().

### Constraints
*   **Boolean Masks**: When using Flash Attention, the `sequence_id` must be a boolean mask [esm/models/esmc.py:156-158]().
*   **Attention Weights**: Flash Attention does not support returning attention weights. If `output_attentions=True` is requested, the model must fall back to standard `MultiHeadAttention` [esm/models/esmc.py:152-155]().

Sources:
- [esm/layers/attention.py:99-143]()
- [esm/models/esmc.py:151-165]()

---

## Model Outputs: ESMCOutput

The model returns an `ESMCOutput` dataclass containing the following fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `sequence_logits` | `torch.Tensor` | Logits over the amino acid vocabulary. |
| `embeddings` | `torch.Tensor` | Final hidden state of the model. |
| `hidden_states` | `torch.Tensor` | A stack of hidden states from all transformer layers. |
| `attentions` | `tuple[torch.Tensor]` | (Optional) Attention maps if Flash Attention is disabled. |

Sources:
- [esm/models/esmc.py:37-42]()

---

## Pretrained Factory & Variants

The `ESMC.from_pretrained` factory function provides a unified interface for loading different model scales.

### Loading a Model
```python
# Example: Loading the 600M variant
model = ESMC.from_pretrained("esmc_600m", device="cuda")
```

### Supported Variants
The model scale is determined by the `d_model`, `n_heads`, and `n_layers` parameters passed to the `ESMC` constructor during the loading process via `load_local_model` [esm/models/esmc.py:80-96](). Common variants include:
*   **ESMC 300M**
*   **ESMC 600M** (Default) [esm/utils/constants/models.py:10]()
*   **ESMC 6B**

Sources:
- [esm/models/esmc.py:79-96]()
- [esm/pretrained.py]()
- [esm/utils/constants/models.py:10]()

---

## SDK Interface Implementation

`ESMC` implements the `ESMCInferenceClient` interface, providing high-level methods for protein analysis:

*   **`encode(input: ESMProtein)`**: Converts an `ESMProtein` object into an `ESMProteinTensor` by tokenizing the sequence [esm/models/esmc.py:193-202]().
*   **`decode(input: ESMProteinTensor)`**: Converts tensors back into an `ESMProtein` object [esm/models/esmc.py:204-213]().
*   **`logits(...)`**: Returns the sequence logits for a given protein tensor, supporting both single and batched inputs [esm/models/esmc.py:215-224]().

Sources:

# Page: ESMFold2 – All-Atom Structure Prediction

# ESMFold2 – All-Atom Structure Prediction

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [cookbook/tutorials/binder_design.ipynb](cookbook/tutorials/binder_design.ipynb)
- [cookbook/tutorials/esmc_sae_feature_interpretation.ipynb](cookbook/tutorials/esmc_sae_feature_interpretation.ipynb)
- [esm/models/esmfold2/conformers.py](esm/models/esmfold2/conformers.py)
- [esm/models/esmfold2/constants.py](esm/models/esmfold2/constants.py)
- [esm/models/esmfold2/output.py](esm/models/esmfold2/output.py)
- [esm/models/esmfold2/paired_msa.py](esm/models/esmfold2/paired_msa.py)
- [esm/models/esmfold2/prepare_input.py](esm/models/esmfold2/prepare_input.py)
- [esm/models/esmfold2/processor.py](esm/models/esmfold2/processor.py)
- [esm/models/esmfold2/types.py](esm/models/esmfold2/types.py)
- [esm/utils/constants/models.py](esm/utils/constants/models.py)

</details>



ESMFold2 is a diffusion-based structure prediction pipeline designed for high-accuracy all-atom modeling of proteins, nucleic acids, and small molecule ligands. Unlike the original ESMFold which used a folding trunk to predict coordinates directly, ESMFold2 leverages a generative approach to handle complex hetero-complexes and multi-chain assemblies.

## Pipeline Overview

The ESMFold2 pipeline follows a structured flow from high-level sequence and constraint definitions to low-level tensor representations, culminating in a diffusion-based structure generation process.

### Code Entity Space to System Flow
The following diagram bridges the high-level input types to the internal processing classes used to prepare data for the model.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Input Space (StructurePredictionInput)"
        PI["ProteinInput"]
        DI["DNAInput"]
        RI["RNAInput"]
        LI["LigandInput"]
    end

    SPI["StructurePredictionInput"] --> CLEAN["clean_esmfold2_input"]
    CLEAN --> BUILDER["ESMFold2InputBuilder"]
    
    subgraph "Internal Processing"
        BUILDER --> PREP["prepare_esmfold2_input"]
        PREP --> CCD["load_ccd"]
        PREP --> MSA_PROC["construct_paired_msa"]
    end

    PREP --> TENSORS["Feature Tensors (torch.Tensor)"]
    PREP --> CINFO["list[ChainInfo]"]

    TENSORS --> MODEL["ESMFold2 Model Forward"]
    CINFO --> OUTPUT["build_molecular_complex_from_features"]
```
Sources: [esm/models/esmfold2/processor.py:143-186](), [esm/models/esmfold2/prepare_input.py:1-5]()

## Input Specification

The entry point for all predictions is the `StructurePredictionInput` dataclass. It serves as a container for sequences, Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSAs), and spatial conditioning.

### Support for Hetero-complexes
ESMFold2 supports a variety of molecular inputs defined in `esm.models.esmfold2.types`:
*   **`ProteinInput`**: Supports amino acid sequences, MSAs, and post-translational `Modification` objects [esm/models/esmfold2/types.py:11-19]().
*   **`DNAInput` / `RNAInput`**: Supports nucleic acid sequences [esm/models/esmfold2/types.py:14-18]().
*   **`LigandInput`**: Supports small molecules defined by Chemical Component Dictionary (CCD) codes [esm/models/esmfold2/types.py:15-19]().

### Conditioning and Constraints
Predictions can be guided by external information:
*   **`DistogramConditioning`**: Provides distance constraints between specific atoms [esm/models/esmfold2/types.py:13-19]().
*   **`CovalentBond`**: Explicitly defines bonds between entities, such as protein-ligand linkages [esm/models/esmfold2/types.py:12-19]().

## Input Preparation & Tokenization

The `ESMFold2InputBuilder` orchestrates the conversion of high-level inputs into model-ready tensors.

### The Cleaning Phase
Before tokenization, `clean_esmfold2_input` handles sequence normalization. It expands polyprotein sequences (separated by `|`) into individual `ProteinInput` objects and groups identical sequences to optimize the MSA representation [esm/models/esmfold2/processor.py:86-181](). This function also converts `|` chainbreak tokens to `:` in the sequence and raises an error if `covalent_bonds` are provided with chainbreaks [esm/models/esmfold2/processor.py:94-112]().

### Atom and Token Generation
The core logic resides in `prepare_esmfold2_input`. This function iterates through the provided sequences to build two primary metadata lists:
1.  **`TokenInfo`**: Metadata for every residue or atom-token (in the case of ligands/modifications), tracking `asym_id`, `entity_id`, and `res_type` [esm/models/esmfold2/prepare_input.py:81-93]().
2.  **`AtomInfo`**: Detailed metadata for every atom, including element symbols, atomic numbers, and idealized coordinates retrieved from the CCD [esm/models/esmfold2/prepare_input.py:68-78]().

The `tokenize_protein` function handles protein sequences, applying modifications and generating tokens and atoms. Modified residues are atom-tokenized (one token per atom), while standard residues produce one token with all heavy atoms [esm/models/esmfold2/prepare_input.py:190-205](). Similarly, `tokenize_dna`, `tokenize_rna`, and `tokenize_ligand` handle their respective molecule types.

### CCD Conformer Loading
For ligands and modified residues, ESMFold2 uses the Chemical Component Dictionary (CCD). The `load_ccd` utility downloads or loads a serialized RDKit-based dictionary to provide "Computed" or "Ideal" coordinates for atom-level initialization [esm/models/esmfold2/conformers.py:36-76](). The `get_idealized_atom_pos` and `get_ligand_idealized_atom_pos` functions retrieve these positions based on residue type or name and atom name [esm/models/esmfold2/conformers.py:155-192]().

Sources: [esm/models/esmfold2/prepare_input.py:176-203](), [esm/models/esmfold2/processor.py:143-152]()

## Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA)

ESMFold2 utilizes paired MSAs for multi-chain protein complexes. The `construct_paired_msa` function is responsible for this process [esm/models/esmfold2/paired_msa.py:105-105]().

| Feature | Implementation |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Taxonomy Pairing** | Uses `key=N` tokens in FASTA headers to pair sequences from the same organism [esm/models/esmfold2/paired_msa.py:3-7](). The `_taxonomy_from_header` function extracts this information [esm/models/esmfold2/paired_msa.py:35-39]().
| **Block-Diagonalization** | Unpaired sequences are placed in chain-specific blocks to prevent false inter-chain correlations [esm/models/esmfold2/paired_msa.py:192-200]().
| **Insertion Handling** | Strips lowercase letters and `.` from A3M formats, storing them as `deletion_count` [esm/models/esmfold2/paired_msa.py:42-78](). The `msa_to_res_type_and_deletions` function performs this conversion [esm/models/esmfold2/paired_msa.py:42-87]().

The `construct_paired_msa` function takes `chain_msas`, `chain_query_res_types`, `token_asym_ids`, and `token_res_ids` as input to build the final MSA features [esm/models/esmfold2/paired_msa.py:105-120](). It returns `msa_residues`, `deletion_value`, and `is_paired` arrays [esm/models/esmfold2/paired_msa.py:125-130]().

Sources: [esm/models/esmfold2/paired_msa.py:86-121]()

## Output Construction

After the model performs the forward pass (diffusion sampling), the raw coordinate tensors must be mapped back to a structured molecular format.

### MolecularComplex Assembly
The `build_molecular_complex_from_features` function performs the following steps:
1.  **Filtering**: Applies the `atom_mask` to remove non-existent or unpredicted atoms [esm/models/esmfold2/output.py:33-37]().
2.  **Mapping**: Uses `chain_infos` (the metadata generated during input prep) to assign atoms to their respective residues and chains [esm/models/esmfold2/output.py:52-56]().
3.  **Ligand Collapse**: For non-polymer chains (`MOL_TYPE_NONPOLYMER`), it collapses multiple atom-tokens into a single residue entry for the final `MolecularComplex` [esm/models/esmfold2/output.py:57-82]().
4.  **Confidence Extraction**: Maps per-token pLDDT scores from the model back to the residues [esm/models/esmfold2/output.py:92-94]().

### Result Mapping
The output is encapsulated in a `MolecularComplex`, which provides methods for exporting to PDB or mmCIF formats via `esm.utils.structure.molecular_complex`.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class StructurePredictionInput {
        +list sequences
        +DistogramConditioning distogram_conditioning
        +list covalent_bonds
    }
    class ESMFold2InputBuilder {
        +prepare_input(input)
    }
    class MolecularComplex {
        +np.ndarray atom_positions
        +np.ndarray plddt
        +list sequence
        +to_pdb()
        +to_mmcif()
    }
    StructurePredictionInput --|> ProteinInput
    StructurePredictionInput --|> DNAInput
    StructurePredictionInput --|> RNAInput
    StructurePredictionInput --|> LigandInput
    ESMFold2InputBuilder ..> StructurePredictionInput : processes
    ESMFold2InputBuilder ..> MolecularComplex : produces via output.py
```

Sources: [esm/models/esmfold2/output.py:18-126](), [esm/models/esmfold2/processor.py:10-18]()

---

# Page: VQ-VAE Structure Tokenizer & Function Decoder

# VQ-VAE Structure Tokenizer & Function Decoder

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [esm/layers/codebook.py](esm/layers/codebook.py)
- [esm/layers/geom_attention.py](esm/layers/geom_attention.py)
- [esm/layers/rotary.py](esm/layers/rotary.py)
- [esm/layers/structure_proj.py](esm/layers/structure_proj.py)
- [esm/models/function_decoder.py](esm/models/function_decoder.py)
- [esm/models/vqvae.py](esm/models/vqvae.py)
- [esm/pretrained.py](esm/pretrained.py)
- [esm/tokenization/__init__.py](esm/tokenization/__init__.py)

</details>



The ESM3 ecosystem utilizes specialized discrete latent spaces for protein structure and functional annotations. These are implemented via a Vector Quantized Variational Autoencoder (VQ-VAE) for structural coordinates and a Multi-Head Decoder for functional keywords and InterPro entries. These components allow ESM3 to treat structure and function as discrete token tracks alongside the primary amino acid sequence.

## Structural Tokenization (VQ-VAE)

The structural tokenization system converts 3D atomic coordinates into a sequence of discrete tokens and back again. This is achieved through the `StructureTokenEncoder` and `StructureTokenDecoder` classes defined in `esm/models/vqvae.py`.

### StructureTokenEncoder
The encoder maps 3D coordinates (represented as `Affine3D` objects and `Atom37` tensors) into a discrete latent space. It utilizes a `GeometricEncoderStack` which is a transformer variant where every layer is a `UnifiedTransformerBlock` configured for geometric attention [esm/models/vqvae.py:142-160](). The `GeometricEncoderStack` inherits from `TransformerStack` but overrides the `blocks` attribute to use `UnifiedTransformerBlock` with `use_geom_attn=True` and `use_plain_attn=False` [esm/models/vqvae.py:142-157]().

**Key Components:**
- **Geometric Attention**: Uses `GeometricReasoningOriginalImpl` to compute attention weights based on both rotation and distance between residues [esm/layers/geom_attention.py:9-31]().
- **K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN)**: The encoder operates on a graph constructed from the 16 nearest neighbors for each residue [esm/models/vqvae.py:191]().
- **EMA Codebook**: A `EMACodebook` containing 4096 codes (`n_codes`) of dimension 128 (`d_out`) performs the vector quantization [esm/models/vqvae.py:187](). The `EMACodebook` manages a set of learnable embeddings and uses Exponential Moving Average (EMA) for updating them [esm/layers/codebook.py:8-33]().
- **RelativePositionEmbedding**: Used to embed relative positional information between residues [esm/models/vqvae.py:188]().

### StructureTokenDecoder
The decoder performs the inverse operation: reconstructing 3D backbone coordinates from discrete structural tokens. It is a significantly larger model than the encoder (30 layers vs 2 layers in the standard configuration) [esm/pretrained.py:44](). The decoder also uses a `TransformerStack` for processing the token embeddings [esm/models/vqvae.py:240-248]().

**Output Heads:**
- **Dim6RotStructureHead**: Predicts the 6D representation (Graham-Schmidt) of rotations and 3D translations to reconstruct the protein backbone [esm/layers/structure_proj.py:8-25]().
- **PairwisePredictionHead**: Predicts distograms and pLDDT/pTM metrics [esm/models/vqvae.py:52-70](). This head takes the output of the transformer and projects it to predict pairwise distances and other structural metrics.
- **RegressionHead**: Used for predicting pLDDT and pTM values [esm/models/vqvae.py:98-111]().

### Structure Data Flow Diagram

The following diagram illustrates the flow from physical coordinates to the discrete "Code Entity Space" (tokens) and back to reconstructed structure.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural Language Space (Physical Structure)"
        A["Protein Coordinates (Atom37)"]
    end

    subgraph "Structure Encoding Pipeline"
        B["build_affine3d_from_coordinates"]
        C["StructureTokenEncoder (esm.models.vqvae.StructureTokenEncoder)"]
        D["GeometricEncoderStack (esm.models.vqvae.GeometricEncoderStack)"]
        E["EMACodebook (esm.layers.codebook.EMACodebook)"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space (Tokens)"
        F["Structure Tokens (Discrete)"]
    end

    subgraph "Structure Decoding Pipeline"
        G["StructureTokenDecoder (esm.models.vqvae.StructureTokenDecoder)"]
        H["TransformerStack (esm.layers.transformer_stack.TransformerStack)"]
        I["Dim6RotStructureHead (esm.layers.structure_proj.Dim6RotStructureHead)"]
        J["PairwisePredictionHead (esm.models.vqvae.PairwisePredictionHead)"]
        K["RegressionHead (esm.models.vqvae.RegressionHead)"]
    end

    subgraph "Natural Language Space (Reconstructed Structure)"
        L["Reconstructed Affine3D & Coordinates"]
        M["Predicted pLDDT/pTM"]
    end

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G
    G --> H
    H --> I
    H --> J
    H --> K
    I --> L
    J --> M
    K --> M
```
Sources: [esm/models/vqvae.py:142-220](), [esm/layers/structure_proj.py:8-63](), [esm/utils/structure/affine3d.py:10-20](), [esm/layers/codebook.py:8-33](), [esm/models/vqvae.py:230-300]()

---

## Function Token Decoder

The `FunctionTokenDecoder` is responsible for translating the discrete function tokens generated by ESM3 into human-readable InterPro annotations and keyword descriptions. Function tokens are depth-8 LSH (Locality Sensitive Hashing) encoded representations [esm/models/function_decoder.py:54-125](). The `FunctionTokenDecoderConfig` [esm/models/function_decoder.py:22-52]() defines parameters such as `d_model`, `n_heads`, `n_layers`, `function_token_vocab_size`, `function_token_depth`, `num_interpro_classes`, and `keyword_vocabulary_size`.

### Architecture
The decoder consists of a `TransformerStack` that processes the function tokens and three specialized regression heads [esm/models/function_decoder.py:92-125]():
1.  **interpro_logits**: A `RegressionHead` predicting the presence of 29,026 InterPro classes [esm/models/function_decoder.py:119-123](). The InterPro IDs are loaded from a CSV file specified in `interpro_entry_list` [esm/models/function_decoder.py:63-69]().
2.  **keyword_logits**: A binary classification head for 58,641 keywords [esm/models/function_decoder.py:107-111](). The keyword vocabulary is loaded from a file specified by `keyword_vocabulary_path` [esm/models/function_decoder.py:71-73]().
3.  **keyword_tfidf**: A head that regresses the TF-IDF value of present keywords to determine their relative importance [esm/models/function_decoder.py:112-116]().

The `TransformerStack` [esm/models/function_decoder.py:92-103]() uses `d_model`, `n_heads`, and `n_layers` from the configuration. An `nn.Embedding` layer maps the input `token_ids` to embeddings before being passed to the transformer [esm/models/function_decoder.py:85-91]().

### LSH Bit Unpacking
Function tokens are typically stored as integers. The decoder can "unpack" these into single-bit tokens to provide distinct embeddings for each bit in the LSH signature [esm/models/function_decoder.py:141-163](). This is controlled by the `unpack_lsh_bits` configuration parameter [esm/models/function_decoder.py:44](). If `unpack_lsh_bits` is `True`, the input `token_ids` are treated as LSH values, and individual bits are extracted and shifted into distinct vocabulary ranges for embedding. Otherwise, a depth-position offset is applied to the `token_ids` to ensure distinct embeddings for tokens at different depths [esm/models/function_decoder.py:164-171]().

### Function Mapping Diagram

This diagram shows how the model bridges the gap between high-dimensional functional keywords and the discrete token space used by the ESM3 transformer.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Code Entity Space (Tensors)"
        T1["Function Tokens (Depth-8) (token_ids)"]
    end

    subgraph "FunctionTokenDecoder (esm.models.function_decoder.FunctionTokenDecoder)"
        D1["unpack_lsh_bits (if config.unpack_lsh_bits)"]
        D2["nn.Embedding (embedding)"]
        D3["TransformerStack (decoder)"]
        D4["RegressionHead (heads.interpro_logits)"]
        D5["RegressionHead (heads.keyword_logits)"]
        D6["RegressionHead (heads.keyword_tfidf)"]
    end

    subgraph "Natural Language Space (Annotations)"
        A1["InterPro ID (e.g., IPR001234)"]
        A2["Functional Keywords (e.g., 'DNA-binding')"]
        A3["TF-IDF Values"]
    end

    T1 --> D1
    D1 --> D2
    D2 --> D3
    D3 --> D4
    D3 --> D5
    D3 --> D6
    D4 --> A1
    D5 --> A2
    D6 --> A3
```
Sources: [esm/models/function_decoder.py:104-125](), [esm/models/function_decoder.py:141-171](), [esm/tokenization/function_tokenizer.py:15-20]()

---

## Pretrained Factory Functions

The VQ-VAE and Function Decoder are instantiated and loaded via factory functions in `esm/pretrained.py`. These functions handle the initialization of empty weights, loading of local `.pth` files, and mapping to the correct device [esm/pretrained.py:28-63]().

| Factory Function | Class | d_model | n_layers | n_heads | v_heads | d_out | n_codes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ESM3_structure_encoder_v0` | `StructureTokenEncoder` | 1024 | 2 | 1 | 128 | 128 | 4096 |
| `ESM3_structure_decoder_v0` | `StructureTokenDecoder` | 1280 | 30 | 20 | N/A | N/A | N/A |
| `ESM3_function_decoder_v0` | `FunctionTokenDecoder` | 1024 | 3 | 8 | N/A | N/A | N/A |

These components are integrated into the full ESM3 model during its construction in `ESM3_sm_open_v0`, where they are passed as function pointers (`structure_encoder_fn`, `structure_decoder_fn`, `function_decoder_fn`) [esm/pretrained.py:108-119](). The `LOCAL_MODEL_REGISTRY` [esm/pretrained.py:128-136]() maps string identifiers to these factory functions, allowing for dynamic loading via `load_local_model` [esm/pretrained.py:139-150]().

### Implementation Details Table

| Feature | Structure Tokenizer | Function Decoder |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Quantization** | EMA Codebook (4096 codes) [esm/models/vqvae.py:187]() | LSH (Depth 8, 8 bits/token) [esm/models/function_decoder.py:44-52]() |
| **Attention Type** | Geometric (Rotation/Distance) [esm/models/vqvae.py:142-157]() | Plain Transformer (GELU) [esm/models/function_decoder.py:101]() |
| **Primary Class** | `StructureTokenEncoder`/`StructureTokenDecoder` [esm/models/vqvae.py:179-230]() | `FunctionTokenDecoder` [esm/models/function_decoder.py:54]() |
| **Vocab Size** | 4096 (codebook size) [esm/models/vqvae.py:187]() | ~260 (per depth) [esm/models/function_decoder.py:31]() |
| **Source File** | `esm/models/vqvae.py` | `esm/models/function_decoder.py` |

Sources: [esm/pretrained.py:28-150](), [esm/models/vqvae.py:1-192](), [esm/models/function_decoder.py:21-125]()
