# Page: Tokenization System

# Tokenization System

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [esm/models/vqvae.py](esm/models/vqvae.py)
- [esm/tokenization/__init__.py](esm/tokenization/__init__.py)
- [esm/tokenization/tokenizer_base.py](esm/tokenization/tokenizer_base.py)

</details>



The ESM repository utilizes a multi-track tokenization architecture to represent proteins across different modalities. Instead of a single sequence-based tokenizer, the system employs a collection of specialized tokenizers that handle sequence, structure, secondary structure, solvent accessibility (SASA), and functional annotations. This modularity allows ESM3 to process and generate multimodal protein data in a unified latent space.

The core of this system is defined in `esm/tokenization/__init__.py`, which provides the `TokenizerCollection` and the `TokenizerCollectionProtocol` to manage these tracks.

### Multi-Track Architecture

The `TokenizerCollection` aggregates the specific tokenizers required for the model's various input tracks. For ESM3 models, the `get_esm3_model_tokenizers` function initializes a complete set of these tokenizers [esm/tokenization/__init__.py:34-43]().

| Track | Tokenizer Class | Responsibility |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Sequence** | `EsmSequenceTokenizer` | Amino acid sequences and special tokens like chain breaks [esm/tokenization/sequence_tokenizer.py:10](). |
| **Structure** | `StructureTokenizer` | VQ-VAE based structural tokens [esm/tokenization/__init__.py:17](). |
| **Secondary Structure** | `SecondaryStructureTokenizer` | SS8 or SS3 classification [esm/tokenization/__init__.py:18](). |
| **SASA** | `SASADiscretizingTokenizer` | Discretized solvent accessibility bins [esm/tokenization/__init__.py:19](). |
| **Function** | `InterProQuantizedTokenizer` | LSH-quantized functional annotations [esm/tokenization/__init__.py:20](). |
| **Residue** | `ResidueAnnotationsTokenizer` | Per-residue specific annotations [esm/tokenization/__init__.py:21](). |

### Code Entity Relationship: Tokenizer Protocols

The system relies on structural typing via Python `Protocols` to ensure consistency across different tokenizer implementations. The `EsmTokenizerBase` defines the standard interface for special tokens (mask, bos, eos, pad) and the fundamental `encode`/`decode` methods [esm/tokenization/tokenizer_base.py:5-26]().

**Tokenizer Collection Registry**
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        TC["TokenizerCollection (dataclass)"]
        TCP["TokenizerCollectionProtocol (Protocol)"]
        GET_ESM3["get_esm3_model_tokenizers()"]
        BASE["EsmTokenizerBase (Protocol)"]
    end

    subgraph "Per-Track Tokenizers"
        SEQ["EsmSequenceTokenizer"]
        STR["StructureTokenizer"]
        SS["SecondaryStructureTokenizer"]
        SASA["SASADiscretizingTokenizer"]
        FUNC["InterProQuantizedTokenizer"]
        RES["ResidueAnnotationsTokenizer"]
    end

    GET_ESM3 --> TC
    TC -.-> TCP
    TC --> SEQ
    TC --> STR
    TC --> SS
    TC --> SASA
    TC --> FUNC
    TC --> RES
    
    SEQ -.-> BASE
    STR -.-> BASE
    SS -.-> BASE
    SASA -.-> BASE
    FUNC -.-> BASE
    RES -.-> BASE
```
**Sources:** [esm/tokenization/__init__.py:15-32](), [esm/tokenization/tokenizer_base.py:5-26]()

### Sequence Tokenization
The `EsmSequenceTokenizer` is a character-level tokenizer built on the HuggingFace `tokenizers` library using a Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) model with no merges [esm/tokenization/sequence_tokenizer.py:10-32](). It handles the standard 20 amino acids plus special tokens:
* `<cls>`: Start of sequence [esm/tokenization/sequence_tokenizer.py:49]().
* `<eos>`: End of sequence [esm/tokenization/sequence_tokenizer.py:49]().
* `|`: Chain break token for multi-chain proteins [esm/tokenization/sequence_tokenizer.py:24]().
* `<mask|pad|unk>`: Standard MLM tokens.

For details, see [Sequence & Secondary Structure Tokenizers](#5.1).

### Structural & Functional Tracks
While the sequence track uses standard NLP-style tokenization, other tracks use specialized discretization:
* **Structure:** Uses a VQ-VAE to map 3D coordinates into discrete tokens. The `StructureTokenEncoder` [esm/models/vqvae.py:179]() is responsible for encoding local structure into these tokens.
* **Function:** Uses Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH) to quantize InterPro functional annotations into a depth-8 hierarchical encoding.

For details, see [Function & Residue Annotation Tokenizers](#5.2).

### Token Management Utilities
The system includes utility functions to handle special token IDs across different tracks. For instance, `get_invalid_tokenizer_ids` retrieves tokens that should typically be excluded from sampling or loss calculations (mask, pad, cls, eos) [esm/tokenization/__init__.py:52-66]().

**Data Flow: From Protein to Multi-Track Tokens**
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Natural Language / Bio Space"
        PROT["Protein Sequence & Structure"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        COLL["TokenizerCollection"]
        SEQ_T["EsmSequenceTokenizer"]
        STR_T["StructureTokenizer"]
        FUNC_T["InterProQuantizedTokenizer"]
    end

    PROT --> COLL
    COLL -->|Amino Acids| SEQ_T
    COLL -->|3D Coordinates| STR_T
    COLL -->|InterPro Terms| FUNC_T
    
    SEQ_T -->|ID: 5| T1["Sequence Tokens"]
    STR_T -->|ID: 402| T2["Structure Tokens"]
    FUNC_T -->|ID: 1024| T3["Function Tokens"]
```
**Sources:** [esm/tokenization/__init__.py:34-43](), [esm/tokenization/sequence_tokenizer.py:17-43]()

---
**Child Pages:**
* [Sequence & Secondary Structure Tokenizers](#5.1)
* [Function & Residue Annotation Tokenizers](#5.2)

# Page: Sequence & Secondary Structure Tokenizers

# Sequence & Secondary Structure Tokenizers

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [esm/tokenization/residue_tokenizer.py](esm/tokenization/residue_tokenizer.py)
- [esm/tokenization/sasa_tokenizer.py](esm/tokenization/sasa_tokenizer.py)
- [esm/tokenization/sequence_tokenizer.py](esm/tokenization/sequence_tokenizer.py)
- [esm/tokenization/ss_tokenizer.py](esm/tokenization/ss_tokenizer.py)
- [esm/tokenization/structure_tokenizer.py](esm/tokenization/structure_tokenizer.py)

</details>



This page documents the tokenization system for sequence and structural tracks in ESM. The system is built around a common protocol, `EsmTokenizerBase`, which ensures consistency across different data modalities including amino acid sequences, secondary structure classifications, and discretized surface accessibility values.

## Tokenization Architecture

The ESM tokenization system uses a multimodal approach where different tracks (sequence, structure, SASA, etc.) are tokenized independently before being processed by the transformer.

### EsmTokenizerBase Protocol
All tokenizers in the ESM ecosystem implement the `EsmTokenizerBase` protocol. This ensures that every tokenizer provides a consistent interface for special tokens and basic operations like encoding and decoding.

**Interface Overview:**
*   **Special Tokens**: Every tokenizer must provide `mask`, `bos`, `eos`, `pad`, and `chain_break` tokens and their corresponding integer IDs [esm/tokenization/tokenizer_base.py:5-15]().
*   **Methods**: Implementations must provide `encode()` and `decode()` methods [esm/tokenization/tokenizer_base.py:17-19]().
*   **Properties**: `all_token_ids` and `special_token_ids` are required for sampling and masking logic [esm/tokenization/tokenizer_base.py:21-25]().

### Sequence & Structure Tokenization Flow
The following diagram illustrates how raw protein data is transformed into tokens by the various tokenizer classes.

**Data to Token Entity Mapping**
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural Language & Biological Space"
        AA_SEQ["Amino Acid Sequence 'MKT...'"]
        SS_STR["SS8 String 'GHH...'"]
        SASA_VALS["SASA Floats [12.5, 0.0, ...]"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        EST["EsmSequenceTokenizer"]
        SST["SecondaryStructureTokenizer"]
        SDT["SASADiscretizingTokenizer"]
        
        SEQ_TOK["sequence_tokens (Tensor)"]
        SS_TOK["secondary_structure_tokens (Tensor)"]
        SASA_TOK["sasa_tokens (Tensor)"]
    end

    AA_SEQ -->|encode| EST
    SS_STR -->|encode| SST
    SASA_VALS -->|encode| SDT

    EST --> SEQ_TOK
    SST --> SS_TOK
    SDT --> SASA_TOK

    style EST stroke-dasharray: 5 5
    style SST stroke-dasharray: 5 5
    style SDT stroke-dasharray: 5 5
```
Sources: [esm/tokenization/sequence_tokenizer.py:10-15](), [esm/tokenization/ss_tokenizer.py:10-13](), [esm/tokenization/sasa_tokenizer.py:9-12]()

---

## EsmSequenceTokenizer

The `EsmSequenceTokenizer` is the primary tokenizer for amino acid sequences. It inherits from `PreTrainedTokenizerFast` (HuggingFace) and uses a character-level Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) model with no merges [esm/tokenization/sequence_tokenizer.py:10-31]().

### Configuration and Vocab
*   **Vocabulary**: Based on `C.SEQUENCE_VOCAB` [esm/tokenization/sequence_tokenizer.py:27-28]().
*   **Special Tokens**: Includes `<unk>`, `<cls>`, `<pad>`, `<mask>`, `<eos>`, and the chain break token `|` [esm/tokenization/sequence_tokenizer.py:18-24]().
*   **Post-Processing**: Automatically wraps single sequences in `<cls>` and `<eos>` tokens using `TemplateProcessing` [esm/tokenization/sequence_tokenizer.py:48-54]().

### Chain Breaks
The tokenizer handles multi-chain proteins using the `|` character. This is mapped to a specific `chain_break_token_id` to inform the model of discontinuities in the polypeptide backbone [esm/tokenization/sequence_tokenizer.py:24-41]().

Sources: [esm/tokenization/sequence_tokenizer.py:10-64]()

---

## SecondaryStructureTokenizer

The `SecondaryStructureTokenizer` handles the discretization of protein secondary structure into either 8-class (SS8) or 3-class (SS3) representations [esm/tokenization/ss_tokenizer.py:13-15]().

### Supported Vocabularies
| Kind | Vocabulary Source | Tokens |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **SS8** | `C.SSE_8CLASS_VOCAB` | G, H, I, T, E, B, S, C [esm/tokenization/ss_tokenizer.py:26]() |
| **SS3** | `C.SSE_3CLASS_VOCAB` | H, E, C [esm/tokenization/ss_tokenizer.py:28]() |

### Implementation Details
*   **Special Tokens**: Uses `<pad>`, `<motif>`, and `<unk>`. Notably, for secondary structure, `<pad>` is used for BOS, EOS, and Chainbreak roles [esm/tokenization/ss_tokenizer.py:80-117]().
*   **Encoding**: Maps characters directly to indices in the concatenated list of special and non-special tokens [esm/tokenization/ss_tokenizer.py:33-67]().

Sources: [esm/tokenization/ss_tokenizer.py:10-126]()

---

## SASADiscretizingTokenizer

The `SASADiscretizingTokenizer` converts continuous Solvent Accessible Surface Area (SASA) values into discrete bins.

### Discretization Logic
*   **Bins**: Uses 15 discretization boundaries defined in `C.SASA_DISCRETIZATION_BOUNDARIES` [esm/tokenization/sasa_tokenizer.py:12]().
*   **Bucketing**: Uses `torch.bucketize` to map float values into discrete ranges [esm/tokenization/sasa_tokenizer.py:79-80]().
*   **Midpoints**: For decoding, the tokenizer maintains a `midpoints_tensor` to map discrete tokens back to a representative float value (the center of the bin) [esm/tokenization/sasa_tokenizer.py:34-42]().

### Vocabulary Structure
The vocabulary consists of special tokens followed by range tokens formatted as `<low-high>` (e.g., `<0-2.5>`) [esm/tokenization/sasa_tokenizer.py:26-31]().

Sources: [esm/tokenization/sasa_tokenizer.py:9-106]()

---

## StructureTokenizer (VQ-VAE Wrapper)

The `StructureTokenizer` is a convenience class designed to provide access to special token IDs used by the `StructureTokenEncoder` and `StructureTokenDecoder` (the VQ-VAE system) [esm/tokenization/structure_tokenizer.py:5-7]().

### VQ-VAE Special Tokens
Because structure tokens represent latent codes from a VQ-VAE codebook, they do not have string representations. The tokenizer defines special IDs starting after the codebook size [esm/tokenization/structure_tokenizer.py:9-16]().

| Token Name | ID Calculation |
| :--- | :--- |
| **MASK** | `codebook_size` |
| **EOS** | `codebook_size + 1` |
| **BOS** | `codebook_size + 2` |
| **PAD** | `codebook_size + 3` |
| **CHAINBREAK** | `codebook_size + 4` |

**Note**: Calling `encode()` or `decode()` on this class will raise a `NotImplementedError`, as structure encoding requires 3D coordinates and the VQ-VAE model [esm/tokenization/structure_tokenizer.py:71-83]().

Sources: [esm/tokenization/structure_tokenizer.py:5-83]()

---

The following diagram shows how the tokenizer classes relate to the base protocol and the underlying utilities.

Sources: [esm/tokenization/tokenizer_base.py:4-26](), [esm/tokenization/sequence_tokenizer.py:10](), [esm/tokenization/ss_tokenizer.py:10](), [esm/tokenization/sasa_tokenizer.py:9](), [esm/tokenization/structure_tokenizer.py:5]()

# Page: Function & Residue Annotation Tokenizers

# Function & Residue Annotation Tokenizers

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [LICENSE.md](LICENSE.md)
- [esm/data/ParentChildTreeFile.txt](esm/data/ParentChildTreeFile.txt)
- [esm/data/entry_list_safety_29026.list](esm/data/entry_list_safety_29026.list)
- [esm/data/interpro_29026_to_keywords_58641.csv](esm/data/interpro_29026_to_keywords_58641.csv)
- [esm/data/keyword_idf_safety_filtered_58641.npy](esm/data/keyword_idf_safety_filtered_58641.npy)
- [esm/data/keyword_vocabulary_safety_filtered_58641.txt](esm/data/keyword_vocabulary_safety_filtered_58641.txt)
- [esm/tokenization/function_tokenizer.py](esm/tokenization/function_tokenizer.py)
- [esm/utils/constants/esm3.py](esm/utils/constants/esm3.py)
- [esm/utils/function/encode_decode.py](esm/utils/function/encode_decode.py)
- [esm/utils/function/interpro.py](esm/utils/function/interpro.py)
- [esm/utils/function/lsh.py](esm/utils/function/lsh.py)
- [esm/utils/function/tfidf.py](esm/utils/function/tfidf.py)
- [esm/utils/types.py](esm/utils/types.py)

</details>



The ESM3 model family utilizes specialized tokenization tracks to represent protein function and site-specific residue annotations. Unlike sequence or structure tokens, these tokenizers handle sparse, multi-label, and hierarchical biological data by mapping InterPro accessions and functional keywords into a discrete token space suitable for transformer architectures.

## 1. InterProQuantizedTokenizer

The `InterProQuantizedTokenizer` is responsible for converting high-level functional descriptions (InterPro IDs and keywords) into a multi-token representation. It employs a Locality Sensitive Hashing (LSH) approach to compress high-dimensional TF-IDF vectors into a depth-8 sequence of discrete tokens [esm/tokenization/function_tokenizer.py:30-35]().

### 1.1 Implementation & Data Flow
The tokenizer transforms functional annotations into tokens through a multi-stage pipeline:
1.  **TF-IDF Vectorization**: Keywords associated with an InterPro ID or free-text annotations are converted into a sparse vector using a precomputed vocabulary and Inverse Document Frequency (IDF) weights [esm/tokenization/function_tokenizer.py:120-124]().
2.  **LSH Hashing**: The TF-IDF vector is projected through multiple hyperplanes. Each projection generates a bit, and groups of bits are combined to form a token ID [esm/utils/function/lsh.py:23-31]().
3.  **Depth-8 Encoding**: To capture the complexity of functional space, the tokenizer produces 8 tokens per position (depth=8), allowing the model to attend to different functional facets simultaneously [esm/tokenization/function_tokenizer.py:59-60]().

### 1.2 System Architecture Diagram
The following diagram illustrates the flow from raw biological labels to the quantized token indices used by the ESM3 `TransformerStack`.

**Function Tokenization Pipeline**
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        A["InterPro ID (e.g., IPR000008)"]
        B["Functional Keywords"]
    end

    subgraph "esm.utils.function"
        C["interpro.InterPro"]
        D["tfidf.TFIDFModel"]
        E["lsh.LSHTokenized"]
    end

    subgraph "esm.tokenization"
        F["InterProQuantizedTokenizer"]
    end

    A --> C
    C -- "Lookup Keywords" --> B
    B --> D
    D -- "Sparse Vector" --> E
    E -- "Depth-8 Hashing" --> F
    F -- "Token IDs" --> G["ESM3 Input Track"]
```
Sources: [esm/tokenization/function_tokenizer.py:30-90](), [esm/utils/function/tfidf.py:13-33](), [esm/utils/function/lsh.py:33-72]()

---

## 2. ResidueAnnotationsTokenizer

The `ResidueAnnotationsTokenizer` handles site-specific annotations, such as active sites, binding sites, or post-translational modifications (PTMs). Unlike the functional tokenizer which describes global or domain-level properties, this tokenizer maps labels to specific residue indices [esm/tokenization/residue_tokenizer.py:15-20]().

### 2.1 Multi-Label Handling
Since a single residue can have multiple annotations (e.g., both a binding site and a phosphorylation site), the tokenizer represents these as a set of labels per position.
*   **Vocabulary**: Tokens are prefixed with `<ra:...>` and contain comma-separated internal IDs [esm/tokenization/residue_tokenizer.py:152-158]().
*   **Encoding**: The `encode` method produces a tensor of shape `(length, max_annotations)`, where `max_annotations` (default 16) defines the maximum number of simultaneous labels tracked per residue [esm/tokenization/residue_tokenizer.py:167-178]().

**Residue Annotation Data Mapping**
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Input Data (Sample)"
        DESC["interpro_site_descriptions"]
        START["interpro_site_starts"]
        RES["interpro_site_residues"]
    end

    subgraph "ResidueAnnotationsTokenizer"
        MAP["_description2id"]
        VOCAB["vocab_to_index"]
    end

    DESC --> MAP
    START -->|Index Alignment| POS["Positional ID Set"]
    MAP --> POS
    POS -->|Join| TOK["<ra:id1,id2>"]
    TOK -->|Padding| TENSOR["torch.Tensor (L, 16)"]

    RES -->|Sanity Check| VALID["Sequence Mismatch Check"]
```
Sources: [esm/tokenization/residue_tokenizer.py:73-158](), [esm/tokenization/residue_tokenizer.py:167-183]()

---

## 3. Supporting Utilities

### 3.1 InterPro Hierarchy (`interpro.py`)
The `InterPro` class manages the ontology and metadata. It parses the `ParentChildTreeFile.txt` to build a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of functional relationships [esm/utils/function/interpro.py:94-107]().
*   **Entry Types**: Categorizes IDs into `FAMILY`, `DOMAIN`, `ACTIVE_SITE`, etc. [esm/utils/function/interpro.py:57-79]().
*   **Graph Utility**: Uses `networkx.DiGraph` to navigate parent-child relationships between functional terms [esm/utils/function/interpro.py:164-178]().

### 3.2 TF-IDF Vectorization (`tfidf.py`)
The `TFIDFModel` mimics the behavior of `scikit-learn`'s TfidfVectorizer with sublinear scaling.
*   **Encoding**: Converts a list of terms into a `scipy.sparse.csr_matrix` [esm/utils/function/tfidf.py:34-54]().
*   **Normalization**: Vectors are L2-normalized to ensure consistent input for the LSH projection [esm/utils/function/tfidf.py:50]().

### 3.3 Locality Sensitive Hashing (`lsh.py`)
The `LSHTokenized` class implements the quantization logic.
*   **Hyperplanes**: Random (or pre-trained) hyperplanes are used to partition the vector space [esm/utils/function/lsh.py:8-22]().
*   **Multi-Table**: Supports multiple LSH tables to generate the depth-8 token representation required by the function tokenizer [esm/utils/function/lsh.py:33-62]().

| Component | File Path | Key Class/Logic |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Function Tokenizer** | `esm/tokenization/function_tokenizer.py` | `InterProQuantizedTokenizer` |
| **Residue Tokenizer** | `esm/tokenization/residue_tokenizer.py` | `ResidueAnnotationsTokenizer` |
| **Ontology Manager** | `esm/utils/function/interpro.py` | `InterPro` (Graph-based) |
| **Vector Space** | `esm/utils/function/tfidf.py` | `TFIDFModel` (Sparse vectors) |
| **Quantization** | `esm/utils/function/lsh.py` | `LSHTokenized` (Bitstream to Tokens) |

Sources: [esm/tokenization/function_tokenizer.py:30-46](), [esm/tokenization/residue_tokenizer.py:15-20](), [esm/utils/function/interpro.py:94-100](), [esm/utils/function/tfidf.py:13-18](), [esm/utils/function/lsh.py:33-41]()

---

# Page: Encoding, Decoding & Generation Pipeline

# Encoding, Decoding & Generation Pipeline

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [esm/utils/decoding.py](esm/utils/decoding.py)
- [esm/utils/encoding.py](esm/utils/encoding.py)
- [esm/utils/generation.py](esm/utils/generation.py)
- [esm/utils/sampling.py](esm/utils/sampling.py)

</details>



The ESM3 ecosystem revolves around a unified pipeline that converts high-level protein descriptions into discrete tensor representations, performs iterative generation via masked language modeling, and decodes those tensors back into physically realizable protein structures and annotations. This lifecycle is managed by the `ESM3InferenceClient` and supported by specialized utility modules in `esm.utils`.

### High-Level Pipeline Flow

The pipeline operates across three primary stages:
1.  **Encoding**: Converting an `ESMProtein` object (containing sequences, coordinates, and labels) into an `ESMProteinTensor` using track-specific tokenizers and VQ-VAE encoders.
2.  **Generation**: Using the transformer backbone to fill in masked tokens across multiple tracks (sequence, structure, function, etc.) through iterative sampling.
3.  **Decoding**: Converting the predicted `ESMProteinTensor` back into an `ESMProtein` object, which involves backbone reconstruction from structure tokens and keyword extraction from function tokens.

### Data Flow Diagram

The following diagram maps the conceptual pipeline stages to the specific code entities and data structures used in the ESM repository.

**Pipeline Entity Mapping**
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Input Space"
        P["ESMProtein (esm/sdk/api.py)"]
    end

    subgraph "Encoding Logic (esm/utils/encoding.py)"
        TE["StructureTokenEncoder (esm/models/vqvae.py)"]
        TC["TokenizerCollection (esm/tokenization/collection.py)"]
        EF["encode_function_annotations (esm/utils/function/encode_decode.py)"]
    end

    subgraph "Tensor Space"
        EPT["ESMProteinTensor (esm/sdk/api.py)"]
    end

    subgraph "Generation Logic (esm/utils/generation.py)"
        IS["iterative_sampling_raw (esm/utils/generation.py)"]
        SL["sample_logits (esm/utils/sampling.py)"]
        NS["NOISE_SCHEDULE_REGISTRY (esm/utils/noise_schedules.py)"]
    end

    subgraph "Decoding Logic (esm/utils/decoding.py)"
        TD["StructureTokenDecoder (esm/models/vqvae.py)"]
        FD["FunctionTokenDecoder (esm/models/function_decoder.py)"]
        DPT["decode_protein_tensor (esm/utils/decoding.py)"]
    end

    P -->|encode| TC
    TC --> TE
    TE --> EF
    EF --> EPT
    EPT --> IS
    IS --> SL
    SL --> NS
    NS --> EPT
    EPT -->|decode| DPT
    DPT --> TD
    DPT --> FD
    TD --> P
    FD --> P
```
**Sources:** [esm/sdk/api.py:11-21](), [esm/utils/encoding.py:144-152](), [esm/utils/decoding.py:31-36](), [esm/utils/generation.py:99-103]()

---

### 6.1 Encoding Proteins into Tensors
The encoding phase transforms human-readable protein data into the discrete multi-track format required by ESM3. This process involves:
*   **Sequence Tokenization**: Mapping amino acids to vocabulary indices using `tokenize_sequence` [esm/utils/encoding.py:35-45]().
*   **Structure Quantization**: Using the `StructureTokenEncoder` [esm/models/vqvae.py:6]() via `tokenize_structure` [esm/utils/encoding.py:48-97]() to map 3D coordinates into discrete structure tokens.
*   **Function Encoding**: Converting `FunctionAnnotation` objects into multi-depth tensors using `encode_function_annotations` [esm/utils/function/encode_decode.py:13-19]() and `tokenize_function_annotations` [esm/utils/encoding.py:138-152]().
*   **Special Tokens**: Automatic addition of `BOS` (Beginning of Sequence) and `EOS` (End of Sequence) tokens to every track, as seen in `get_default_sequence_tokens` [esm/utils/encoding.py:156-169]().

For details, see [Encoding Proteins into Tensors](#6.1).

**Sources:** [esm/utils/encoding.py:35-45](), [esm/models/vqvae.py:6](), [esm/utils/encoding.py:48-97](), [esm/utils/function/encode_decode.py:13-19](), [esm/utils/encoding.py:138-152](), [esm/utils/encoding.py:156-169]()

---

### 6.2 Decoding Tensors Back to Proteins
Decoding is the inverse process, reconstructing physical properties from model outputs. Key components include:
*   **Backbone Reconstruction**: The `StructureTokenDecoder` [esm/models/vqvae.py:10]() converts structure tokens back into 3D coordinates via `decode_structure` [esm/utils/decoding.py:138-169](). The pipeline then uses `ProteinChain.infer_oxygen()` [esm/utils/decoding.py:168]() to complete the backbone.
*   **Annotation Merging**: `decode_function_tokens` [esm/utils/function/encode_decode.py:84-91]() uses a `FunctionTokenDecoder` [esm/models/function_decoder.py:9]() to convert high-dimensional logits into a list of `FunctionAnnotation` objects.
*   **Metric Extraction**: The decoder extracts confidence metrics like `pLDDT`, `pTM`, and `PAE` directly from the structure decoder's output [esm/utils/decoding.py:159-165]().

For details, see [Decoding Tensors Back to Proteins](#6.2).

**Sources:** [esm/models/vqvae.py:10](), [esm/utils/decoding.py:138-169](), [esm/utils/decoding.py:168](), [esm/utils/function/encode_decode.py:84-91](), [esm/models/function_decoder.py:9](), [esm/utils/decoding.py:159-165]()

---

### 6.3 Iterative Masked Generation
Generation in ESM3 is an iterative process where the model unmasks tokens over a series of steps. The `iterative_sampling_raw` function [esm/utils/generation.py:99-128]() orchestrates this by:
*   **Noise Scheduling**: Determining the unmasking rate using schedules like `cosine`, `linear`, or `cubic` from the `NOISE_SCHEDULE_REGISTRY` [esm/utils/noise_schedules.py:1]().
*   **Multi-Track Sampling**: Simultaneously sampling sequence, structure, and function tracks using functions like `sample_logits` [esm/utils/sampling.py:153-197](), `sample_function_logits` [esm/utils/sampling.py:201-206](), and `sample_residue_annotation_logits` [esm/utils/sampling.py:208-213]() while maintaining consistency between them.
*   **Temperature Control**: Applying sampling temperatures defined in `SamplingTrackConfig` [esm/sdk/api.py:20]() to control the diversity of the generated proteins.

For details, see [Iterative Masked Generation](#6.3).

**Sources:** [esm/utils/generation.py:99-128](), [esm/utils/noise_schedules.py:1](), [esm/utils/sampling.py:153-197](), [esm/utils/sampling.py:201-206](), [esm/utils/sampling.py:208-213](), [esm/sdk/api.py:20]()

---

This table bridges the high-level pipeline concepts to the specific classes and functions implemented in the codebase.

| Pipeline Stage | Code Entity | File Path |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| **Encoding** | `encode_function_annotations` | [esm/utils/function/encode_decode.py:13]() |
| **Generation** | `iterative_sampling_raw` | [esm/utils/generation.py:99]() |
| **Generation** | `get_sampling_mask` | [esm/utils/sampling.py:29]() |
| **Decoding** | `decode_protein_tensor` | [esm/utils/decoding.py:31]() |
| **Decoding** | `decode_structure` | [esm/utils/decoding.py:138]()

**Sources:** [esm/utils/encoding.py:48-54](), [esm/utils/function/encode_decode.py:13-19](), [esm/utils/generation.py:99-103](), [esm/utils/sampling.py:29](), [esm/utils/decoding.py:31-36](), [esm/utils/decoding.py:138-143]()

# Page: Encoding Proteins into Tensors

# Encoding Proteins into Tensors

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [esm/layers/attention.py](esm/layers/attention.py)
- [esm/utils/encoding.py](esm/utils/encoding.py)
- [esm/utils/generation.py](esm/utils/generation.py)
- [esm/utils/misc.py](esm/utils/misc.py)

</details>



This page documents the technical process of transforming high-level protein representations (sequence, structure, annotations) into the tensor formats required by ESM models. This pipeline involves tokenization across multiple tracks, coordinate handling, and the addition of special tokens (BOS/EOS) to facilitate multimodal transformer processing.

## Overview of the Encoding Pipeline

The encoding process bridges the gap between the `ESMProtein` SDK object and the `ESMProteinTensor` representation. Each biological "track" (Sequence, Structure, Secondary Structure, SASA, Function) is processed by its respective tokenizer or encoder.

### Data Flow: Protein to Tensor

The following diagram illustrates how different protein attributes are routed through specific code entities to produce the final tensorized representation.

**Diagram: ESMProtein to ESMProteinTensor Data Flow**
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural Language & Bio Space"
        P["ESMProtein Object"]
        SEQ["Amino Acid Sequence"]
        STR["3D Coordinates (Atom37)"]
        FUNC["Function Annotations (InterPro)"]
        SS["Secondary Structure (SS8)"]
        SASA["SASA Values"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space (esm/utils/encoding.py)"
        T_SEQ["tokenize_sequence"]
        T_STR["tokenize_structure"]
        T_FUNC["tokenize_function_annotations"]
        T_SS["tokenize_secondary_structure"]
        T_SASA["tokenize_sasa"]
    end

    subgraph "Tokenization & Model Space"
        VQ["StructureTokenEncoder (VQ-VAE)"]
        IP["InterProQuantizedTokenizer"]
        RA["ResidueAnnotationsTokenizer"]
        SASA_TOK["SASADiscretizingTokenizer"]
    end

    P --> SEQ & STR & FUNC & SS & SASA
    SEQ --> T_SEQ
    STR --> T_STR
    FUNC --> T_FUNC
    SS --> T_SS
    SASA --> T_SASA

    T_STR --> VQ
    T_FUNC --> IP & RA
    T_SASA --> SASA_TOK

    VQ --> ST["Structure Tokens"]
    IP --> FT["Function Tokens"]
    RA --> RAT["Residue Annotation Tokens"]
    SASA_TOK --> SASAT["SASA Tokens"]

    T_SEQ --> STEN["Sequence Tokens"]
    T_SS --> SST["SS8 Tokens"]

    STEN & ST & FT & RAT & SST & SASAT --> EPT["ESMProteinTensor"]
```
**Sources:** [esm/utils/encoding.py:35-152](), [esm/sdk/api.py:1-50]()

---

## Structural Encoding

Structure encoding is the most complex part of the pipeline, as it involves converting continuous 3D coordinates into discrete tokens using a pre-trained VQ-VAE.

### `tokenize_structure`
The `tokenize_structure` function converts raw coordinates into structural tokens and processed coordinate tensors [esm/utils/encoding.py:48-54]().
1.  **Coordinate Preparation**: It uses `ProteinChain.from_atom37` to standardize input coordinates [esm/utils/encoding.py:56-58]().
2.  **VQ-VAE Encoding**: The `StructureTokenEncoder` processes the coordinates and residue indices to produce discrete `structure_tokens` [esm/utils/encoding.py:77-79]().
3.  **Padding and Special Tokens**: If `add_special_tokens` is True, the function pads coordinates with `inf` and structure tokens with `mask_token_id`. It then explicitly sets the first and last tokens to `bos_token_id` and `eos_token_id` respectively [esm/utils/encoding.py:85-96]().

**Sources:** [esm/utils/encoding.py:48-97](), [esm/models/vqvae.py:1-50]()

---

## Function and Residue Annotation Encoding

Function annotations are encoded into two distinct tracks: one for high-level InterPro/TF-IDF keywords and another for site-specific residue annotations.

### `encode_function_annotations`
Located in `esm/utils/function/encode_decode.py`, this function performs the following steps:
1.  **Validation**: Ensures annotation indices are 1-indexed and inclusive within the sequence length [esm/utils/function/encode_decode.py:27-30]().
2.  **Label Sorting**: Iterates through `FunctionAnnotation` objects to determine if they belong to `InterProQuantizedTokenizer` (keywords/IPR terms) or `ResidueAnnotationsTokenizer` (site-specific labels) [esm/utils/function/encode_decode.py:34-49]().
3.  **Tokenization**:
    *   `ft_annotations` are passed to the function tokenizer to create a `(length, depth)` tensor [esm/utils/function/encode_decode.py:54-59]().
    *   `ra_annotations` are processed into residue annotation IDs [esm/utils/function/encode_decode.py:62-79]().

**Sources:** [esm/utils/function/encode_decode.py:13-81](), [esm/tokenization/function_tokenizer.py:1-50]()

---

## Default Token Generation

When specific tracks are missing (e.g., in unconditional generation or when only a sequence is provided), the system generates "default" tokens consisting of mask tokens bounded by BOS and EOS markers.

| Helper Function | Track | Logic |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `get_default_sequence_tokens` | Sequence | `[BOS] + [MASK] * L + [EOS]` [esm/utils/encoding.py:156-169]() |
| `get_default_structure_tokens` | Structure | `[BOS] + [MASK] * L + [EOS]` [esm/utils/encoding.py:172-182]() |
| `get_default_secondary_structure_tokens` | SS8 | `[BOS] + [MASK] * L + [EOS]` [esm/utils/encoding.py:185-194]() |
| `get_default_sasa_tokens` | SASA | `[BOS] + [MASK] * L + [EOS]` [esm/utils/encoding.py:197-206]() |

**Sources:** [esm/utils/encoding.py:156-206]()

---

## Tensor Concatenation and Padding

The final step of encoding involves assembling the individual track tensors into a single batch.

### `stack_variable_length_tensors`
This utility handles the creation of batches from proteins of different lengths.
*   **Logic**: It determines the maximum dimensions across the batch and pads shorter sequences with a `constant_value` (usually 0 or a specific pad token) [esm/utils/misc.py:180-209]().
*   **Data Flow**: `[L1, D], [L2, D] -> [Batch, Max_L, D]` [esm/utils/misc.py:193-195]().

**Diagram: Batch Tensor Construction**
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Input Sequences"
        S1["Seq 1 (Length 10)"]
        S2["Seq 2 (Length 15)"]
    end

    subgraph "esm/utils/misc.py"
        SVL["stack_variable_length_tensors"]
    end

    subgraph "Output Tensor"
        BT["Batched Tensor (Shape: 2, 15, D)"]
        P1["Seq 1 + 5 Padding Steps"]
        P2["Seq 2 (No Padding)"]
    end

    S1 & S2 --> SVL
    SVL --> BT
    BT --> P1 & P2
```
**Sources:** [esm/utils/misc.py:180-209]()

---

## Key Utility Functions

*   **`rbf`**: Computes Radial Basis Function encodings for distances, used in geometric featurization [esm/utils/misc.py:105-115]().
*   **`knn_graph`**: Constructs a K-Nearest Neighbors graph based on 3D coordinates, with fallbacks to sequence distance when coordinates are missing or masked [esm/utils/misc.py:135-177]().
*   **`slice_any_object`**: A polymorphic slicer that handles lists, strings, numpy arrays, and torch tensors uniformly, essential for manipulating protein fragments during encoding [esm/utils/misc.py:74-102]().

**Sources:** [esm/utils/misc.py:74-177]()

---

# Page: Decoding Tensors Back to Proteins

# Decoding Tensors Back to Proteins

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [esm/utils/decoding.py](esm/utils/decoding.py)
- [esm/utils/sampling.py](esm/utils/sampling.py)

</details>



The decoding pipeline is the inverse of the tokenization process, transforming discrete multi-track tensors back into human-readable protein representations. This process involves structural reconstruction from VQ-VAE latent codes, merging hierarchical function annotations, and extracting confidence metrics such as pLDDT and PAE.

## The Decoding Lifecycle

The primary entry point for this process is `decode_protein_tensor` [esm/utils/decoding.py:31-36](). This function orchestrates the conversion of an `ESMProteinTensor`—which contains tokenized tracks for sequence, structure, SASA, secondary structure, and function—into a rich `ESMProtein` object [esm/utils/decoding.py:101-111]().

### Data Flow and Entity Mapping

The following diagram illustrates how the decoding functions map to the specific components of the `ESMProteinTensor` and which model entities are responsible for the transformation.

**Tensor to Protein Entity Mapping**
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Tensor Space (ESMProteinTensor)"
        T_SEQ["sequence (Tensor)"]
        T_STR["structure (Tensor)"]
        T_SS["secondary_structure (Tensor)"]
        T_SASA["sasa (Tensor)"]
        T_FUNC["function (Tensor)"]
        T_RES["residue_annotations (Tensor)"]
        T_COORD["coordinates (Tensor)"]
    end

    subgraph "Logic Space (decoding.py)"
        D_SEQ["decode_sequence()"]
        D_STR["decode_structure()"]
        D_SS["decode_secondary_structure()"]
        D_SASA["decode_sasa()"]
        D_FUNC["decode_function_annotations()"]
        D_RES_ANN["decode_residue_annotations()"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space (Models/Tokenizers)"
        M_VQ["StructureTokenDecoder"]
        M_FD["FunctionTokenDecoder"]
        M_PC["ProteinChain"]
        TOK_SEQ["EsmSequenceTokenizer"]
        TOK_SS["SecondaryStructureTokenizer"]
        TOK_SASA["SASADiscretizingTokenizer"]
        TOK_FUNC["InterProQuantizedTokenizer"]
        TOK_RES["ResidueAnnotationsTokenizer"]
    end

    T_SEQ --> D_SEQ
    T_STR --> D_STR
    T_SS --> D_SS
    T_SASA --> D_SASA
    T_FUNC --> D_FUNC
    T_RES --> D_RES_ANN
    T_COORD --> D_STR

    D_SEQ --> TOK_SEQ
    D_STR --> M_VQ
    M_VQ --> M_PC
    D_SS --> TOK_SS
    D_SASA --> TOK_SASA
    D_FUNC --> M_FD
    D_FUNC --> TOK_FUNC
    D_RES_ANN --> TOK_RES
```
**Sources:** [esm/utils/decoding.py:31-111](), [esm/utils/function/encode_decode.py:84-133]()

---

## Structural Reconstruction

Structural decoding is the most complex part of the pipeline, as it involves converting discrete indices back into 3D atomic coordinates.

### StructureTokenDecoder and Oxygen Inference
The `decode_structure` function [esm/utils/decoding.py:138-143]() takes structural tokens and passes them to the `StructureTokenDecoder` [esm/utils/decoding.py:153]().
1. **Backbone Prediction**: The decoder returns backbone coordinates (`bb_pred`) for N, CA, and C atoms [esm/utils/decoding.py:154-156]().
2. **Chain Assembly**: These coordinates are used to initialize a `ProteinChain` via `from_backbone_atom_coordinates` [esm/utils/decoding.py:167]().
3. **Oxygen Inference**: Since the VQ-VAE primarily handles backbone tokens, the carbonyl oxygen (O) positions are geometrically inferred using `chain.infer_oxygen()` [esm/utils/decoding.py:168]().
4. **Final Representation**: The result is a full Atom37 tensor representing the reconstructed backbone [esm/utils/decoding.py:169]().

### Confidence Metrics Extraction
During the decoding of the structure track, the model also provides estimates of its own prediction quality:
* **pLDDT**: Extracted from the decoder output and stripped of BOS/EOS tokens [esm/utils/decoding.py:159-161]().
* **pTM & PAE**: Extracted directly from the decoder's auxiliary heads if available [esm/utils/decoding.py:163-165]().

**Sources:** [esm/utils/decoding.py:138-171](), [esm/utils/structure/protein_chain.py:56-58]()

---

## Function and Residue Annotation Decoding

Function decoding merges two distinct types of data: global/domain-level InterPro annotations and site-specific residue annotations.

### InterPro and Keyword Merging
The `decode_function_annotations` function [esm/utils/decoding.py:89-93]() (which internally calls `decode_function_tokens` [esm/utils/function/encode_decode.py:84-91]()) uses the `FunctionTokenDecoder` to process predicted logits:
1. **Keyword Extraction**: It retrieves predicted function keywords from the decoder [esm/utils/function/encode_decode.py:125]().
2. **InterPro Formatting**: InterPro annotations are decoded and formatted back into standard IPR identifiers (e.g., "IPR001234") using the `InterProQuantizedTokenizer.format_annotation` method [esm/utils/function/encode_decode.py:126-132]().

### Residue Annotation Processing
Residue-level annotations (like active sites or binding regions) are decoded via `decode_residue_annotations` [esm/utils/decoding.py:96-98]() (which internally calls `decode_residue_annotation_tokens` [esm/utils/function/encode_decode.py:136-141]()).
* **Depth Traversal**: The function iterates through the multi-track residue annotation tensor (up to `MAX_RESIDUE_ANNOTATIONS` [esm/utils/sampling.py:12]()) [esm/utils/function/encode_decode.py:158]().
* **Label Mapping**: Token IDs are mapped back to labels using the `ResidueAnnotationsTokenizer.vocabulary` [esm/utils/function/encode_decode.py:164-165]().
* **Merging**: Contiguous residue predictions of the same type are merged into single `FunctionAnnotation` objects using `merge_annotations` [esm/utils/function/encode_decode.py:170]().

**Sources:** [esm/utils/function/encode_decode.py:84-180](), [esm/utils/decoding.py:89-99](), [esm/utils/sampling.py:12]()

---

## Handling Special Tokens and Padding

A critical step in decoding is the removal of structural markers used during model inference.

| Step | Logic | File Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **BOS/EOS Removal** | Slices tokens using `tokens[1:-1]` to remove Start/End markers. | [esm/utils/decoding.py:52]() |
| **Mask Detection** | If a track contains mask tokens, it is treated as `None` to prevent invalid decoding. | [esm/utils/decoding.py:58-61]() |
| **Pad Cleanup** | If a track consists entirely of pad tokens, it is discarded. | [esm/utils/decoding.py:55-56]() |
| **Sequence Cleanup** | Removes whitespace and converts internal mask strings to short format. | [esm/utils/decoding.py:130-131]() |

### Tokenizer Interaction Diagram
This diagram shows how `decode_protein_tensor` interacts with the various tokenizer classes to perform its duties.

**Decoding Interaction Diagram**
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant D as decode_protein_tensor
    participant TC as TokenizerCollectionProtocol
    participant ST as StructureTokenizer
    participant SD as StructureTokenDecoder
    participant FT as InterProQuantizedTokenizer
    participant FD as FunctionTokenDecoder
    participant SEQ_T as EsmSequenceTokenizer
    participant SS_T as SecondaryStructureTokenizer
    participant SASA_T as SASADiscretizingTokenizer
    participant RES_T as ResidueAnnotationsTokenizer

    D->>TC: Get track tokenizers (sequence, structure, etc.)
    loop For each track in ESMProteinTensor
        D->>D: Remove BOS/EOS tokens [esm/utils/decoding.py:52]()
        D->>TC: Check for pad_token_id [esm/utils/decoding.py:55]()
        alt Track is all pad tokens
            D->>D: Set track to None
        end
        alt Track is structure and contains mask tokens
            D->>D: Set track to None [esm/utils/decoding.py:58-61]()
        end
    end

    alt Sequence track is present
        D->>SEQ_T: decode(sequence_tokens) [esm/utils/decoding.py:64-65]()
        SEQ_T-->>D: decoded_sequence_string
    end

    alt Structure track is present
        D->>SD: decode(structure_tokens) [esm/utils/decoding.py:69-72]()
        SD-->>D: bb_pred, plddt, ptm, pae
        D->>ProteinChain: from_backbone_atom_coordinates(bb_pred, sequence) [esm/utils/decoding.py:167]()
        ProteinChain->>ProteinChain: infer_oxygen() [esm/utils/decoding.py:168]()
        ProteinChain-->>D: atom37_positions
    else Coordinates track is present
        D->>D: Use raw coordinates [esm/utils/decoding.py:75-76]()
    end

    alt Secondary structure track is present
        D->>SS_T: decode(secondary_structure_tokens) [esm/utils/decoding.py:79-81]()
        SS_T-->>D: decoded_ss_string
    end

    alt SASA track is present
        D->>SASA_T: decode(sasa_tokens) [esm/utils/decoding.py:83-84]()
        SASA_T-->>D: decoded_sasa_values
    end

    alt Function track is present
        D->>FD: decode(function_tokens) [esm/utils/decoding.py:89-93]()
        FD-->>D: function_keywords, interpro_annotations
        D->>FT: format_annotation()
        FT-->>D: formatted_interpro_ids
    end

    alt Residue annotations track is present
        D->>RES_T: decode(residue_annotation_tokens) [esm/utils/decoding.py:96-98]()
        RES_T-->>D: decoded_residue_annotations
    end

    D->>ESMProtein: __init__(...) [esm/utils/decoding.py:101-111]()
    ESMProtein-->>D: final_protein_object
```

**Sources:** [esm/utils/decoding.py:31-111](), [esm/utils/encoding.py:156-182]()

# Page: Iterative Masked Generation

# Iterative Masked Generation

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [esm/utils/decoding.py](esm/utils/decoding.py)
- [esm/utils/encoding.py](esm/utils/encoding.py)
- [esm/utils/generation.py](esm/utils/generation.py)
- [esm/utils/sampling.py](esm/utils/sampling.py)

</details>



Iterative masked generation is the core mechanism for protein design and refinement in ESM3. Unlike standard autoregressive models that generate sequences from left to right, ESM3 uses a Masked Language Modeling (MLM) approach where tokens across multiple tracks (sequence, structure, function, etc.) are iteratively unmasked and sampled based on a noise schedule.

## Generation Loop Overview

The generation process is orchestrated by two primary functions in `esm/utils/generation.py`: `iterative_sampling_raw` and `iterative_sampling_tokens`. These functions manage the transition from masked inputs to fully realized protein designs by repeatedly calling the model's forward pass and sampling from the resulting logits.

### Key Components
*   **Noise Schedules**: Define the rate at which tokens are unmasked over the course of the generation steps.
*   **Sampling Strategies**: Determine how to select the next set of tokens to unmask (e.g., random vs. lowest entropy).
*   **Track-Specific Logic**: Custom handling for different modalities like InterPro function tokens or SASA.

### Data Flow Diagram
The following diagram illustrates how the `iterative_sampling_tokens` function bridges the high-level `ESM3InferenceClient` with the underlying tensor manipulations.

**Iterative Sampling Data Flow**
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "SDK / User Space"
        P["ESMProtein"]
        C["GenerationConfig"]
    end

    subgraph "Generation Logic (esm/utils/generation.py)"
        IST["iterative_sampling_tokens"]
        BPT["_BatchedESMProteinTensor"]
        NS["Noise Schedule (cosine/linear)"]
    end

    subgraph "Inference Space"
        IC["ESM3InferenceClient.forward_and_sample"]
        LOGITS["Logits / Samples"]
    end

    P -->|encode| IST
    C --> IST
    IST --> BPT
    BPT -->|batch loop| IC
    IC -->|output| LOGITS
    LOGITS -->|update| BPT
    NS -->|calculate mask| IST
    BPT -->|decode| P_OUT["Generated ESMProtein"]
```
Sources: [esm/utils/generation.py:100-128](), [esm/utils/generation.py:228-310](), [esm/sdk/api.py:340-360]()

## Noise Schedules and Unmasking

The generation process proceeds over $T$ steps. At each step, a fraction of the currently masked tokens is selected for unmasking. The number of tokens to unmask is determined by a noise schedule registered in `NOISE_SCHEDULE_REGISTRY` [esm/utils/noise_schedules.py:1-10]().

| Schedule | Description | Implementation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Linear** | Constant number of tokens unmasked per step. | `linear_schedule` |
| **Cosine** | Follows a cosine curve; fewer tokens unmasked at the start/end. | `cosine_schedule` |
| **Cubic** | Aggressive unmasking in the middle of the trajectory. | `cubic_schedule` |

### Unmasking Strategies
When choosing which specific tokens to unmask at step $t$, the system supports two primary strategies defined in `get_sampling_mask` [esm/utils/sampling.py:246-270]():
1.  **Random**: Tokens are selected uniformly at random from the current mask.
2.  **Entropy-based**: The model's confidence (negative entropy) is used to pick the tokens it is most "certain" about first.

Sources: [esm/utils/generation.py:270-285](), [esm/utils/sampling.py:246-270]()

## Track-Specific Sampling Logic

ESM3 is multimodal, and different tracks require different sampling treatments. These are handled by specialized functions in `esm/utils/sampling.py`.

### Sequence and Structure
Standard tracks use `sample_logits`, which supports temperature scaling and `top_p` (nucleus) sampling [esm/utils/sampling.py:153-198]().
*   **Temperature Annealing**: Often used to reduce randomness as generation progresses.
*   **Invalid ID Masking**: Prevents the model from sampling special tokens like `<pad>` or `<cls>` during generation [esm/utils/sampling.py:177-180]().

### Function and Residue Annotations
*   **Function (InterPro)**: Uses `sample_function_logits`. Since function tokens are hierarchical (depth 8), the sampler must handle multi-dimensional output and a `p_none_threshold` to decide if a residue has no annotation [esm/utils/sampling.py:200-220](). The `InterProQuantizedTokenizer` is used for this track [esm/tokenization/function_tokenizer.py]().
*   **Residue Annotations**: Uses `sample_residue_annotation_logits` to handle the binary/multi-label nature of site annotations [esm/utils/sampling.py:223-243]().

Sources: [esm/utils/sampling.py:153-243](), [esm/utils/generation.py:320-350](), [esm/tokenization/function_tokenizer.py]()

## Batching and Error Handling

The `iterative_sampling_tokens` implementation uses a specialized internal class, `_BatchedESMProteinTensor`, to manage heterogeneous protein lengths in a single GPU batch.

### The `_BatchedESMProteinTensor` Class
This class extends `ESMProteinTensor` to add batch dimensions and provides utilities for slicing and updating specific proteins within a batch [esm/utils/sampling.py:42-108](). It includes methods like `from_protein_tensor` to convert a single `ESMProteinTensor` into a batched one, `slice` to extract a single protein's tensors, and `set_slice` to update a specific protein's data within the batch [esm/utils/sampling.py:45-94](). The `_non_batched_dims` helper function determines the expected number of non-batch dimensions for each track, which is crucial for correct tensor manipulation [esm/utils/sampling.py:17-40]().

**Tensor Management Logic**
```mermaid
classDiagram
    class ESMProteinTensor {
        +Tensor sequence
        +Tensor structure
        +Tensor coordinates
        +...
    }
    class _BatchedESMProteinTensor {
        +batch_size: int
        +from_protein_tensor(protein: ESMProteinTensor) ESMProteinTensor
        +slice(i: int, sequence_len: int | None) ESMProteinTensor
        +set_slice(i: int, slice: ESMProteinTensor)
        +__len__() int
        +_detect_attribute(fn, name) Any
        +_non_batched_dims(k: str, v: torch.Tensor) int
    }
    class GenerationConfig {
        +track: str
        +num_steps: int
        +temperature: float
        +...
    }
    ESMProteinTensor <|-- _BatchedESMProteinTensor
    _BatchedESMProteinTensor ..> GenerationConfig : controlled by
```
Sources: [esm/utils/sampling.py:42-108](), [esm/utils/sampling.py:17-40]()

### Error Handling
During iterative generation, individual proteins in a batch may fail (e.g., due to length constraints or remote API timeouts). The `iterative_sampling_raw` function handles these by appending `ESMProteinError` objects to the output list. If a specific index in the batch fails, the system continues generating for the remaining proteins, ensuring that a single failure does not crash a large batch job [esm/utils/generation.py:118-121](). The `iterative_sampling_tokens` function also includes a `try-except` block to catch `ESMProteinError` during the batch processing and mark the corresponding protein as failed [esm/utils/generation.py:250-265]().

Sources: [esm/utils/sampling.py:42-108](), [esm/utils/generation.py:100-128](), [esm/utils/generation.py:250-265]()

## Implementation Detail: `iterative_sampling_tokens`

The primary entry point for complex generation tasks is `iterative_sampling_tokens` [esm/utils/generation.py:228-310]().

1.  **Initialization**: It converts a list of `ESMProtein` objects into a `_BatchedESMProteinTensor` and prepares the `SamplingConfig` [esm/utils/generation.py:238-245](). It also initializes the `current_tokens` with masked inputs using `_make_masked_inputs` and `_stack_protein_tensors` [esm/utils/generation.py:239-245]().
2.  **Step Loop**:
    *   Calculates the `mask_ratio` based on the current step and the chosen `noise_schedule` [esm/utils/generation.py:270-272]().
    *   Calls `client.forward_and_sample` to get the model's predictions for all tracks [esm/utils/generation.py:290-295]().
    *   Determines which tokens to "keep" (unmask) using `get_sampling_mask` [esm/utils/generation.py:280-285]().
    *   Updates the batch tensor with the newly sampled tokens, applying temperature annealing if specified [esm/utils/generation.py:300-305]().
3.  **Finalization**: Once all steps are complete, the resulting tensors are decoded back into `ESMProtein` objects using `client.decode` [esm/utils/generation.py:310-315](). The `_trim_sequence_tensor_dataclass` utility is used to remove padding before decoding [esm/utils/generation.py:37-60]().

Sources: [esm/utils/generation.py:228-310](), [esm/utils/sampling.py:246-270](), [esm/utils/generation.py:37-60]()

---

# Page: MSA Utilities

# MSA Utilities

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [esm/models/esmfold2/paired_msa.py](esm/models/esmfold2/paired_msa.py)
- [esm/sdk/base_forge_client.py](esm/sdk/base_forge_client.py)
- [esm/utils/msa/__init__.py](esm/utils/msa/__init__.py)
- [esm/utils/msa/filter_sequences.py](esm/utils/msa/filter_sequences.py)
- [esm/utils/msa/msa.py](esm/utils/msa/msa.py)
- [esm/utils/msa/msa_test.py](esm/utils/msa/msa_test.py)
- [esm/utils/parsing.py](esm/utils/parsing.py)

</details>



The Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA) utilities provide a robust framework for handling, filtering, and processing protein sequence alignments. These utilities support core ESM operations, including diversity-based sequence selection for MSA Transformer models and taxonomy-based pairing for ESMFold2 multimer structure prediction.

## The MSA Dataclass

The core of the MSA system is the `MSA` class [esm/utils/msa/msa.py:47-196](), a `SequentialDataclass` that provides an object-oriented interface for manipulating alignments. It stores data as a list of `FastaEntry` objects, which contain headers and sequences.

### Key Features and Methods
*   **Factory Methods**: Supports loading from `.a3m` (A3M), `.sto` (Stockholm), and raw sequence lists [esm/utils/msa/msa.py:76-174]().
*   **Serialization**: Implements `to_bytes` and `from_bytes` for efficient storage and transport, preserving both sequences and headers [esm/utils/msa/msa.py:122-160]().
*   **Subselection**: Methods like `select_sequences` and `select_positions` allow for slicing the MSA by rows or columns while maintaining internal consistency [esm/utils/msa/msa.py:200-203]().
*   **Insertion Handling**: Provides `remove_insertions_from_sequence` to strip lowercase letters and dots from A3M formatted sequences [esm/utils/msa/msa.py:23-25]().
*   **Deletion Counts**: The `MSA` class can store per-match-column deletion counts, particularly when loaded from A3M files, which is crucial for ESMFold2's featurization [esm/utils/msa/msa.py:37](). These deletion counts are preserved through slicing, padding, and stacking operations [esm/utils/msa/msa_test.py:87-149]().

### Data Representation
The `MSA` class lazily computes a NumPy character array (`|S1`) of the sequences for high-performance numerical operations [esm/utils/msa/msa.py:177-178]().

| Attribute | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `entries` | `list[FastaEntry]` | Raw header/sequence pairs [esm/utils/msa/msa.py:37](). |
| `deletions` | `np.ndarray | None` | Per-(row, match-column) a3m deletion counts [esm/utils/msa/msa.py:38](). |
| `sequences` | `list[str]` | Property returning all sequence strings [esm/utils/msa/msa.py:40-41](). |
| `headers` | `list[str]` | Property returning all header strings [esm/utils/msa/msa.py:44-45](). |
| `depth` | `int` | Number of sequences in the MSA [esm/utils/msa/msa.py:169-170](). |
| `seqlen` | `int` | Length of the alignment [esm/utils/msa/msa.py:173-174](). |

**Sources:** [esm/utils/msa/msa.py:28-196](), [esm/utils/parsing.py:6-6](), [esm/utils/msa/msa_test.py:87-149]()

---

## Sequence Selection and Filtering

The library provides two primary mechanisms for reducing MSA depth while preserving information: greedy selection and `hhfilter` wrapping.

### Greedy Diversity Selection
The `greedy_select_indices` function [esm/utils/msa/filter_sequences.py:11-45]() implements the algorithm used in the MSA Transformer paper. It iteratively selects sequences that maximize the average Hamming distance to the already selected set.

1.  Start with the query sequence (index 0).
2.  Calculate the Hamming distance between the current set and all remaining sequences using `scipy.spatial.distance.cdist` [esm/utils/msa/filter_sequences.py:38]().
3.  Add the sequence that maximizes the average distance [esm/utils/msa/filter_sequences.py:39]().
4.  Repeat until `num_seqs` is reached.

### HHFilter Wrapper
The `hhfilter` function [esm/utils/msa/filter_sequences.py:48-82]() provides a Python interface to the `hhfilter` binary from the HH-suite. It filters MSAs based on sequence identity, coverage, and diversity. It writes the input sequences to a temporary FASTA file, executes the `hhfilter` command, and then parses the output to return the indices of the filtered sequences [esm/utils/msa/filter_sequences.py:57-82]().

**Sources:** [esm/utils/msa/filter_sequences.py:11-82]()

---

## Paired MSA for ESMFold2

For multimer structure prediction, ESMFold2 requires "paired" MSAs where sequences from different chains are aligned based on their taxonomic origin.

### Taxonomy Extraction
Taxonomy IDs are parsed from FASTA headers using the regex `key=(-?\d+)`. If no key is found, it defaults to `-1` (unpaired) [esm/models/esmfold2/paired_msa.py:35-39]().

### The Pairing Pipeline
The `construct_paired_msa` function [esm/models/esmfold2/paired_msa.py:106-188]() builds the complex MSA features required by the model:

1.  **Per-chain Tables**: For each chain, it converts the `MSA` object into residue type arrays, deletion count arrays, and extracts taxonomy IDs [esm/models/esmfold2/paired_msa.py:137-152]().
2.  **Grouping by Taxonomy**: Sequences from different chains are grouped by their taxonomy ID, excluding the query row and unpaired entries (`key=-1`) [esm/models/esmfold2/paired_msa.py:154-160]().
3.  **Pairing**: Rows are created by combining sequences with matching taxonomy IDs. The function prioritizes taxonomies with more distinct chains [esm/models/esmfold2/paired_msa.py:161-164]().
4.  **Block-Diagonalization**: Sequences that cannot be paired (unpaired or unique to a chain) are placed in the MSA as block-diagonal entries, where the other chain positions are padded with gaps [esm/models/esmfold2/paired_msa.py:1-7]().
5.  **Feature Generation**: Returns `msa_residues` (token IDs), `deletion_value` (insertion counts), and `is_paired` masks [esm/models/esmfold2/paired_msa.py:114-121]().

**Sources:** [esm/models/esmfold2/paired_msa.py:1-188]()

---

## System Integration Diagrams

### MSA Data Flow: From File to Model
This diagram shows how raw MSA files are processed and transformed into the inputs required by structure prediction models like ESMFold2.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural Language Space (Files)"
        A1[".a3m / .sto Files"]
        A2["FASTA Headers 'key=ID'"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space (esm.utils.msa)"
        B1["MSA.from_a3m()"]
        B2["MSA Dataclass"]
        B3["greedy_select_indices()"]
        B4["hhfilter()"]
    end

    subgraph "Structure Prediction (esm.models.esmfold2)"
        C1["construct_paired_msa()"]
        C2["msa_to_res_type_and_deletions()"]
        C3["StructurePredictionInput"]
    end

    A1 --> B1
    B1 --> B2
    B2 --> B3
    B2 --> B4
    B2 --> C2
    A2 --> C1
    C2 --> C1
    C1 --> C3
```
**Sources:** [esm/utils/msa/msa.py:56-71](), [esm/utils/msa/filter_sequences.py:11-45](), [esm/models/esmfold2/paired_msa.py:86-121](), [esm/utils/structure/input_builder.py:75-80]()

### MSA Selection Logic
The following diagram details the interaction between the `MSA` class and the filtering utilities.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant M as MSA Object
    participant F as filter_sequences.py
    participant S as scipy.spatial

    User->>M: select_sequences(indices)
    M->>F: greedy_select_indices(array, num_seqs)
    loop For each sequence to select
        F->>S: cdist(selected, all, 'hamming')
        S-->>F: pairwise_distances
        F->>F: np.argmax(mean_distance)
    end
    F-->>M: selected_indices
    M-->>User: New MSA (subset)
```
**Sources:** [esm/utils/msa/msa.py:184-187](), [esm/utils/msa/filter_sequences.py:11-45]()

---

# Page: Jupyter Widgets & Interactive UI

# Jupyter Widgets & Interactive UI

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [esm/widgets/components/results_visualizer.py](esm/widgets/components/results_visualizer.py)
- [esm/widgets/components/secondary_structure_prompt_selector.py](esm/widgets/components/secondary_structure_prompt_selector.py)
- [esm/widgets/components/sequence_prompt_selector.py](esm/widgets/components/sequence_prompt_selector.py)
- [esm/widgets/utils/clients.py](esm/widgets/utils/clients.py)
- [esm/widgets/views/esm3_generation_launcher.py](esm/widgets/views/esm3_generation_launcher.py)
- [esm/widgets/views/login.py](esm/widgets/views/login.py)
- [esm/widgets/views/prediction.py](esm/widgets/views/prediction.py)

</details>



The `esm.widgets` package provides a comprehensive set of Jupyter-based interactive components for interacting with ESM3 and ESMC models. These widgets facilitate complex tasks such as multi-track protein generation, property prediction, and high-quality 3D visualization directly within a notebook environment. The UI bridges the gap between high-level design intentions (e.g., "design a protein with this motif and this function") and the underlying SDK and model calls.

## System Architecture Overview

The interactive UI is built on `ipywidgets` and follows a modular pattern where views orchestrate specialized components. It interacts with the `ESM3InferenceClient` and `ESMCInferenceClient` to perform computations either locally or via the Biohub Forge platform.

### Component Relationship Diagram
This diagram illustrates how high-level UI views utilize components and SDK clients to process protein data.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "UI Views"
        A["create_esm3_generation_launcher"]
        B["create_prediction_ui"]
        C["create_login_ui"]
    end

    subgraph "Components & Utilities"
        D["SequencePromptSelector"]
        E["SecondaryStructurePromptSelector"]
        F["SASAPromptSelector"]
        G["FunctionAnnotator"]
        H["create_results_visualizer"]
        I["ProteinImporter"]
    end

    subgraph "SDK Layer"
        J["ESM3InferenceClient"]
        K["ESMProtein"]
    end

    A --> D
    A --> E
    A --> F
    A --> G
    A --> I
    A --> H
    B --> I
    B --> H
    C --> J
    D -.-> K
    E -.-> K
    F -.-> K
    G -.-> K
    H -.-> K
    J --> K
```
**Sources:** [esm/widgets/views/esm3_generation_launcher.py:21-122](), [esm/widgets/views/prediction.py:14-41](), [esm/widgets/views/login.py:11-49]()

## Authentication & Client Initialization
Before performing inference, users must initialize a client. The UI provides a unified login interface that handles:
*   **Inference Options:** Choosing between the remote **Forge/Biohub Platform API** (full model access) or **Local** execution (supports `esm3-sm-open-v1`) [esm/widgets/views/login.py:17-24]().
*   **Token Management:** Input and persistence of `ESM_API_KEY` via environment variables [esm/widgets/views/login.py:107-112]().
*   **Client Factory:** Using `get_forge_client` or `get_local_client` to instantiate the appropriate `ESM3InferenceClient` [esm/widgets/views/login.py:143-148]().

For details, see [Authentication & Client Initialization Widgets](#8.1).

**Sources:** [esm/widgets/views/login.py:11-170](), [esm/widgets/utils/clients.py:7-8]()

## Generation & Prediction Views
The UI supports two primary workflows for protein engineering:

### 1. Multimodal Generation
The generation view allows users to "compile" a prompt by specifying a target length and adding constraints across multiple tracks (sequence, structure, function). 
*   **Generation Launcher:** The `create_esm3_generation_launcher` function orchestrates `batch_generate` calls with configurable `GenerationConfig` parameters like `temperature`, `top_p`, and `num_steps` [esm/widgets/views/esm3_generation_launcher.py:54-101]().
*   **Iterative Design:** Users can copy generated results back into the prompt for iterative refinement [esm/widgets/views/esm3_generation_launcher.py:206-212]().

### 2. Sequential Prediction
The `create_prediction_ui` function focuses on a "one-to-many" track pipeline. Given a sequence or structure, it sequentially predicts all other modalities (Structure -> SS8 -> SASA -> Function) using the `client.generate` interface [esm/widgets/views/prediction.py:89-101]().

For details, see [Generation, Prediction & Inverse Folding Views](#8.2).

**Sources:** [esm/widgets/views/esm3_generation_launcher.py:21-122](), [esm/widgets/views/prediction.py:14-160]()

## Prompt Selectors & Results Visualizer
These components handle the data entry and result inspection for `ESMProtein` objects.

### Interactive Data Mapping
This diagram shows how UI components map user interactions to specific `ESMProtein` fields and SDK operations.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "User Interaction"
        UI_Seq["Sequence Prompt Selector"]
        UI_SS["Secondary Structure Prompt Selector"]
        UI_SASA["SASA Prompt Selector"]
        UI_Func["Function Annotator"]
        UI_Struct["Structure Prompt Selector"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entities"
        CE_PM["PromptManager"]
        CE_Seq["create_sequence_prompt_selector"]
        CE_SS["create_secondary_structure_prompt_selector"]
        CE_SASA["create_sasa_prompt_selector"]
        CE_Func["create_function_annotator"]
        CE_Struct["create_structure_prompt_selector"]
        CE_RV["create_results_visualizer"]
        CE_ESMP["ESMProtein"]
    end

    UI_Seq --> CE_Seq
    UI_SS --> CE_SS
    UI_SASA --> CE_SASA
    UI_Func --> CE_Func
    UI_Struct --> CE_Struct

    CE_Seq --> CE_PM
    CE_SS --> CE_PM
    CE_SASA --> CE_PM
    CE_Func --> CE_PM
    CE_Struct --> CE_PM

    CE_PM -->|compiles prompts into| CE_ESMP
    CE_ESMP -->|visualized by| CE_RV
```
**Sources:** [esm/widgets/components/sequence_prompt_selector.py:12-20](), [esm/widgets/components/secondary_structure_prompt_selector.py:13-21](), [esm/widgets/components/results_visualizer.py:21-43]()

### Key Components:
*   **Prompt Selectors:** Components like `create_sequence_prompt_selector` [esm/widgets/components/sequence_prompt_selector.py:12-20]() and `create_secondary_structure_prompt_selector` [esm/widgets/components/secondary_structure_prompt_selector.py:13-21]() allow users to define constraints on specific regions of a protein. These selectors manage ranges and values, often using a `PromptManager` [esm/widgets/utils/prompting.py:11-12]() to collect and organize user inputs.
*   **Function Annotator:** Uses a `pygtrie` to provide auto-suggestions for InterPro tags and TF-IDF keywords, allowing users to apply labels to specific residue ranges.
*   **Results Visualizer:** The `create_results_visualizer` function is a dispatching component that renders generated proteins based on modality [esm/widgets/components/results_visualizer.py:21-43](). It includes 3D structure visualization (colored by pLDDT), sequence alignment views, and SASA/SS8 charts. The `draw_function_annotations` [esm/widgets/utils/drawing/draw_function_annotations.py:11-13]() and `draw_protein_structure` [esm/widgets/utils/drawing/draw_protein_structure.py:11-13]() utilities are used for rendering.
*   **Protein Importer:** A utility for loading reference proteins from PDB IDs or local files to serve as templates for motifs.

For details, see [Prompt Selectors & Results Visualizer](#8.3).

**Sources:** [esm/widgets/components/results_visualizer.py:21-132](), [esm/widgets/utils/drawing/draw_function_annotations.py:11-13](), [esm/widgets/utils/drawing/draw_protein_structure.py:11-13]()

# Page: Authentication & Client Initialization Widgets

# Authentication & Client Initialization Widgets

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [esm/widgets/utils/clients.py](esm/widgets/utils/clients.py)
- [esm/widgets/utils/types.py](esm/widgets/utils/types.py)
- [esm/widgets/views/esm3_generation_launcher.py](esm/widgets/views/esm3_generation_launcher.py)
- [esm/widgets/views/login.py](esm/widgets/views/login.py)
- [esm/widgets/views/prediction.py](esm/widgets/views/prediction.py)

</details>



This page documents the interactive components within `esm.widgets` responsible for managing user authentication and initializing inference clients. These widgets provide a user-friendly interface for choosing between local execution and remote Biohub Platform (Forge) services, handling API key management, and configuring the underlying SDK clients.

## Overview of Initialization Flow

The initialization process follows a structured path from user selection to the instantiation of a functional `ESM3InferenceClient`. The system uses a container pattern to bridge the gap between interactive Jupyter widgets and subsequent notebook code cells.

### Data Flow Diagram: Client Initialization

This diagram illustrates the flow from the Natural Language Space (UI selection) to the Code Entity Space (Client objects).

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural Language Space (UI)"
        "UI_Selection[Select Inference Option]" --> "Forge_Option[Forge/Biohub Platform API]"
        "UI_Selection" --> "Local_Option[Local]"
        "Forge_Option" --> "Token_Input[Enter API Token]"
        "Local_Option" --> "Model_Fixed[esm3-sm-open-v1]"
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space (esm.widgets)"
        "create_login_ui[create_login_ui]" -- "manages" --> "ClientInitContainer[ClientInitContainer]"
        "ClientInitContainer" -- "calls" --> "get_forge_client[get_forge_client]"
        "ClientInitContainer" -- "calls" --> "get_local_client[get_local_client]"
    end

    subgraph "SDK Implementation (esm.sdk)"
        "get_forge_client" --> "ESM3ForgeInferenceClient[ESM3ForgeInferenceClient]"
        "get_local_client" --> "ESM3[ESM3 (Local PyTorch Model)]"
    end

    "Token_Input" -.-> "ESM_API_KEY[os.environ['ESM_API_KEY']]"
    "ESM_API_KEY" -.-> "get_forge_client"
```

**Sources:** [esm/widgets/views/login.py:11-170](), [esm/widgets/utils/clients.py:12-28](), [esm/widgets/utils/types.py:8-8]()

---

## Key Components

### ClientInitContainer
The `ClientInitContainer` is a metadata and callback wrapper defined in `esm.widgets.utils.types`. It acts as a bridge between the widget UI and the notebook's execution environment.
*   **`metadata`**: A dictionary storing user selections, such as the chosen `inference_option` [esm/widgets/views/login.py:117-117]().
*   **`client_init_callback`**: A `partial` function that, when called, returns a fully initialized `ESM3InferenceClient` [esm/widgets/views/login.py:144-148]().

### create_login_ui
The primary entry point for authentication is `create_login_ui` [esm/widgets/views/login.py:11-170](). This function constructs an `ipywidgets.VBox` containing:
1.  **Backend Selector**: A `RadioButtons` widget allowing users to toggle between "Forge/Biohub Platform API" and "Local" [esm/widgets/views/login.py:33-38]().
2.  **API Key Management**: For Forge users, it provides a text input for the `ESM_API_KEY`. It supports setting this key as an environment variable directly from the UI [esm/widgets/views/login.py:109-110]().
3.  **Model Selection**:
    *   **Forge**: Allows entering a specific model name (defaulting to `esm3-open`) [esm/widgets/views/login.py:91-96]().
    *   **Local**: Hardcoded to `esm3-sm-open-v1` as it is the primary open-source model supported for local inference [esm/widgets/views/login.py:85-90]().

**Sources:** [esm/widgets/views/login.py:11-170](), [esm/widgets/utils/types.py:8-8]()

---

## Client Initialization Callbacks

The widgets use utility functions in `esm/widgets/utils/clients.py` to instantiate the appropriate client type based on the UI state.

### get_forge_client
This function initializes a remote client for the Biohub Platform.
*   **Implementation**: It retrieves the `ESM_API_KEY` from environment variables [esm/widgets/utils/clients.py:21-21]().
*   **Return Type**: Returns an instance of `ESM3ForgeInferenceClient` configured with the specified model name and the Biohub API URL (`https://biohub.ai`) [esm/widgets/utils/clients.py:26-28]().

### get_local_client
This function initializes a local instance of the ESM3 model.
*   **Implementation**: It first validates that the user is logged into Hugging Face via `huggingface_hub.whoami()` [esm/widgets/utils/clients.py:13-17]().
*   **Return Type**: Returns a local `ESM3` model instance loaded onto the GPU (`cuda`) using the `from_pretrained` factory method [esm/widgets/utils/clients.py:17-17]().

### Logic Flow: Callback Assignment
When the user clicks the "Start using ESM3" button in the login UI, the `on_start` callback is triggered [esm/widgets/views/login.py:142-162]():

| Selected Option | Callback Assigned | Target Client Class |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Forge/Biohub** | `partial(get_forge_client, forge_model.value)` | `ESM3ForgeInferenceClient` |
| **Local** | `partial(get_local_client)` | `ESM3` (local model) |

**Sources:** [esm/widgets/utils/clients.py:12-28](), [esm/widgets/views/login.py:142-162]()

---

## Widget Interaction & UI State

The login UI dynamically updates based on user interaction via the `on_selection_change` observer [esm/widgets/views/login.py:116-140]().

### UI State Transitions

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Selection Change [on_selection_change]"
        "Init[Initial State]" -- "Select Forge" --> "Forge_UI[Show Token Input + Forge Model]"
        "Init" -- "Select Local" --> "Local_UI[Show Fixed Local Model]"
    end

    subgraph "Authentication [on_forge_login_clicked]"
        "Forge_UI" -- "Input Token" --> "Env_Var[Set ESM_API_KEY]"
        "Env_Var" --> "Logged_In_View[Show Success Message]"
    end
```

### Implementation Details:
*   **Environment Variable Sync**: When `forge_set_as_env` is checked, the token entered in `forge_token_input` is written to `os.environ["ESM_API_KEY"]` [esm/widgets/views/login.py:109-110]().
*   **Persistence**: The UI checks for the existence of `ESM_API_KEY` in the environment upon initialization to determine whether to show the login form or the "already logged in" view [esm/widgets/views/login.py:77-81]().

**Sources:** [esm/widgets/views/login.py:47-82](), [esm/widgets/views/login.py:107-140]()
